dim otherwise. The row only appears once you've earned at least one, so it stays
out of the way for players who haven't reached the Frontier.

Test: frontier_test.mjs (24 — the card renders the symbols row without error). boot
green.

entries.title: overworld: a BP EXCHANGE counter in every Frontier lobby
entries.body:
The BP shop was previously only offered at the end of a run. Now each of the seven
Frontier lobbies has a side attendant (a real lobby NPC) who runs the BP EXCHANGE:
talk to them to open the shop any time, spend BP between challenges. Wired via the
existing FACILITY_LOBBIES table (a new `bp` clerk tile per lobby) and the same
interact() hook as the challenge reception.

Test: frontier_test.mjs (23 — the lobby BP counter opens the shop). boot green.

entries.title: overworld: Frontier Brains + a BP exchange shop
entries.body:
FRONTIER BRAINS — each facility now has its canonical boss (Anabel, Tucker,
Noland, Spenser, Greta, Lucy, Brandon). In the endless facilities the Brain
challenges you at streak 7 (SILVER symbol) and 21 (GOLD) with a tougher, higher-
level team; beating them awards +10 BP and records the symbol (gold outranks
silver, never downgrades).

BP EXCHANGE — spend the Battle Points you earn. A small shop (Rare Candy, the
Choice items, Life Orb, Leftovers, Focus Sash, Full Restore, Max Revive) offered
at the end of every Frontier run: buying deducts the BP cost and adds the item to
your bag; an over-spend is refused. Wired as a proper list menu (mirrors the ferry
menu) with keyboard + tap input.

Test: frontier_test.mjs (22 — Brains named + milestone tiers + symbol ranking; the
shop opens, buys, refuses insufficient BP, and closes). boot green.

entries.title: Battle Factory as a standalone mini-game on the home page
entries.body:
Since the Battle Factory uses RENTAL POKeMON (not your own party), it works with no
save. Added a "Battle Factory" tile to the home page linking to
overworld/?factory=1, which boots straight into a Factory run: it warps to the
Battle Factory, lends you a generated team, and loops back-to-back battles for BP —
"play again?" between runs. A fresh visitor needs no account, region, or party.

The standalone is fully isolated from any real save: savePos is suppressed and the
run never persists a party. Fixing this also uncovered and fixed a latent bug in
the facility framework — healParty() persists, so healing the run team between
bouts was clobbering the real saved party with the (rental) run team; the between-
bout heal is now in-memory (healTeam), and a real party is only saved when it's
genuinely yours.

Test: frontier_test.mjs (14 — the mini-game boots into the Factory, provisions a
rental-ready lead, auto-starts a battle, and never writes an overworld party save).
boot + postgame regression green.

entries.title: overworld: the remaining six Battle Frontier facilities
entries.body:
Generalizes the Battle Tower into all seven Frontier facilities on one shared
streak/BP core. frontier.js gains a FACILITIES table where each facility is a
distinct rule-set our engine can honour:
- BATTLE TOWER   — endless streak, full heal between bouts (the original).
- BATTLE DOME    — a fixed 5-round tournament; sweep it for a bonus BP.
- BATTLE FACTORY — you battle with a generated RENTAL team, not your own party.
- BATTLE PALACE  — endless, NO healing between bouts (endurance).
- BATTLE ARENA   — a fixed 3-round match, no healing; sweep for bonus BP.
- BATTLE PIKE    — endless; some steps are a lucky room (free BP, no battle).
- BATTLE PYRAMID — endless endurance (no heal), tougher foes, double BP.

main.js replaces the Tower-only loop with a generic run loop parameterized by the
facility config (heal / fixed-rounds / rental / level / rooms), plus a
FACILITY_LOBBIES table mapping each lobby's reception counter to its facility, so
talking to any facility's counter starts that challenge. The one champion-gated
"Battle Frontier" ferry reaches every lobby.

Test: frontier_test.mjs (10 — all 7 configured with their distinguishing rules,
each starts with the right config, and the Factory's rental-team battle works).
boot green.

Follow-ups still open: Frontier Brains (facility bosses at streak milestones) and
a BP shop to spend the BP.

entries.title: overworld: post-game P4b — Battle Frontier (Battle Tower MVP)
entries.body:
Brings the orphaned ~80-map Battle Frontier online with a working Battle Tower:
- Reachability: the post-game ferry now offers "Battle Frontier" (champion-gated),
  landing you at the Frontier so you can reach the Battle Tower.
- New frontier.js: opponent generation (genTeam builds distinct, battle-ready
  teams from the species pool at a chosen level) + BP currency (earn/spend/best,
  persisted to magepunk_bp / magepunk_frontier_best).
- The Battle Tower challenge: talk to the lobby reception counter to start a run
  of consecutive singles battles vs generated FRONTIER TRAINERs; each win heals
  you, extends your streak, and earns 1 BP; a loss ends the run. Foes scale to
  your party's level.

Test: frontier_test.mjs (6 — genTeam validity/distinctness, BP earn/spend/refuse,
and that taking the challenge starts a real battle). boot green.

Scope: this is the Battle Tower MVP. The other facilities (Dome/Factory/Palace/
Arena/Pike/Pyramid), Frontier Brains, and a BP shop are follow-ups on this same
streak/BP core.

entries.title: overworld: post-game P4a — Johto 16-badge path + RED as the crown
entries.body:
Turns Johto's JohKanto post-game into a real 16-badge climb:
- A new JOHKANTO badge slice (badges.js) tracks the 8 crystal-Kanto gyms
  separately from the standalone-Kanto game. A JOHTO save beating a JohKanto gym
  (map id MAP_JOHKANTO_*) now fills JOHKANTO, not KANTO — via badgeSliceFor() in
  onTrainerDefeated — toward a 16-badge total, with a "KANTO badges: n/8" toast.
- RED at Mt Silver now requires all 16 badges (Johto Champion + the 8 JohKanto
  gyms), not just the Johto crown — the true post-game crown.
- The MAGNET TRAIN now runs: becoming Johto Champion sets
  EVENT_RESTORED_POWER_TO_KANTO, and runSpecial('MagnetTrain') warps
  Goldenrod <-> JohKanto Saffron stations (a shortcut to the post-game; the land
  route already worked).

Test: postgame_test.mjs (17 — Red waits until 16 badges; the JohKanto slice
counts; a Johto JohKanto-gym win doesn't touch standalone Kanto). quest/
progression/gymstory regression green.

Deferred refinements: gating JohKanto entry behind the Johto crown (currently the
existing 8-badge Route 26 gate) and a 16-badge trainer-card display.

entries.title: overworld: post-game P3 — ferry to the orphaned legendary islands
entries.body:
Adds a champion's SEAGALLOP/EON ferry: the ferry menu now offers post-game island
routes, each gated on being that region's Champion — Sevii Islands (Kanto, opens
the walk to Mt Ember and MOLTRES), Southern Island (LATIOS), Birth Island
(DEOXYS), and Faraway Island (MEW). New LEGENDARY_ENCOUNTERS entries place Latios
/ Deoxys / Mew on their islands at their real object tiles (all champion-gated);
Deoxys had no encounter anywhere before. These map clusters were fully built but
orphaned with no way in.

Test: postgame_test.mjs (14 — Latios/Deoxys/Mew catchable on their islands once
you're Hoenn Champion). Legendary/boot regression green.

entries.title: overworld: post-game P1+P2 — champion return + Regis + Red
entries.body:
Phase 1 (foundation): beating the Champion no longer strands you in the throne
room. After the Hall of Fame text you're warped home to your region's start town,
your party is healed, and the winning team is recorded to a magepunk_hof log. The
DONE quest objective now points at each region's real post-game (Cerulean Cave /
Mt Silver / the Regi chambers). Without this the whole post-game was unreachable.

Phase 2 (per-region payoff):
- HOENN: the three REGIS (Regirock/Regice/Registeel) are now catchable in their
  chambers (Desert Ruins / Island Cave / Ancient Tomb — all already reachable),
  gated on being HOENN Champion.
- JOHTO: RED now spawns atop MT SILVER (SilverCaveRoom3) once you're JOHTO
  Champion — his data was complete but the object was flag-suppressed. Beating him
  records a beat_red honor. Johto's iconic post-game climax.
- KANTO: Mewtwo/Articuno/Zapdos already worked; the champion return makes them
  actually reachable.

Test: postgame_test.mjs (11 — Regis appear only for the Hoenn champion, Red only
for the Johto champion, champion win warps home + heals + records the HoF). No
regressions (boot/legendary/villain/quest green).

entries.title: overworld: authentic per-spot progression blockers (all 3 regions)
entries.body:
Replaces the invisible "The way ahead is sealed. You need the X Badge" corridor
message with real, OG-style physical obstacles at every chokepoint — a gym guide
who turns you back, Team Rocket occupying a city, a sleeping Snorlax, Sudowoodo,
an invisible Kecleon, HM terrain — each cleared by its authentic condition (a
badge, a key item, a story event, or an HM).

New module overworld/blockers.js (the arcade.js/services.js per-map-id injector
pattern, since data/ is read-only): a BLOCKERS table (sprite + solid tiles +
condition + themed line) and a GIVERS table (talk-to NPCs that hand over a key
item once). A blocker is present only while its condition is unmet; meeting it
drops the blocker and the road opens. Wired into player.blocked, interact(), the
render loop, and a new engine.js player.onBump so walking into a blocker shows its
line. HM-terrain chokepoints (the Ilex Forest cut tree) seed via items.js
CODE_FIELD_OBJS and reuse the existing Cut/Rock Smash/Strength pipeline.

The old Quest.blocked gate is kept as a SILENT strand-safety backstop (its dialog
suppressed) — physical blockers stop you first; the backstop only ever fires if a
sprite is mis-placed, guaranteeing no save can strand. Surf/Dive-accessed towns
(Cinnabar, Mossdeep, Ever Grande) had their corridor gate relaxed to the Surf/Dive
badge so there's no invisible off-by-one bounce on open water; their gyms and the
League doors inside stay gated at the right badge (+ the Hoenn climax).

Key items + givers: Poke Flute (Mr. Fuji, after the Rocket Hideout) wakes the two
Kanto Snorlax; Squirtbottle (Goldenrod florist, after Whitney) clears Route 36
Sudowoodo; Devon Scope (Steven, Route 120) reveals the Kecleon bridge.

Strand-safety is proven, not assumed: tests/blockers_test.mjs (70) runs the real
map-reachability graph and asserts no-skip (authentic gates never open a corridor
map earlier than the badge backstop), no-strand, giver-reachability (every key
item is obtainable on the near side before its wall), and an acyclic key-item
dependency graph. tests/blockers_ingame_test.mjs (7, headless) verifies a live
block clears when its condition is met and a giver grants exactly once, with no
client errors. Full regression stays green (boot/quest/quest_reach/villain/
legendary/awakening/intro/dive/gymstory/progression).

No new art — all sprites already shipped.

entries.title: overworld: the Hoenn legendary-awakening plot (Kyogre/Groudon/Rayquaza)
entries.body:
After you beat Archie at the Seafloor Cavern (the Hoenn villain climax), the roused
weather trio tear Hoenn apart until Rayquaza is woken to still them. Six beats play
out across Route 128, Sootopolis, and the Sky Pillar, and you actually SEE Kyogre and
Groudon clashing over Sootopolis — then Rayquaza descending to calm them — rendered on
their real decomp tiles. The catch is unchanged: they're still real battles on their
lair tiles (Sky Pillar / Marine Cave / Terra Cave).

Why a code director rather than the literal decomp scripts: this port can't render
them. The NPC loader skips every flag-gated object, so the story actors (the
legendaries, Steven, Wallace, Archie, Maxie) never spawn; every weather/camera/orb/
battle `special` is a no-op; the port never runs onLoad/onWarp; and the clash and
calming scenes have no dialogue at all — they were pure animation. Run as-is, the chain
would be invisible state changes. So instead a self-contained director, gated on
villain_hoenn_climax and driving its own VAR_HOENN_AWAKENING (the decomp scene vars stay
dormant, so their onFrame scenes never fire), plays authored narration for each beat
and draws the legendaries over Sootopolis at their real object_event positions. As a
side effect it opens the Sky Pillar door (an onLoad the port skips) and clears the
crisis weather flag when it resolves.

Note: the abnormal-weather/camera VFX are not rendered (no weather layer in this port);
the drama is carried by the narration + the on-screen legendary sprites.

Test: awakening_test.mjs (15 — dormant pre-climax, all six beats advance, door walkable,
Rayquaza still catchable, weather clears, no replay). Regression green: villain (47),
quest (71), legendary (30), boot_smoke (5).

entries.title: overworld: the 3 legendary beasts — catchable at Tin Tower
entries.body:
Raikou, Entei, and Suicune are now catchable at the top of Tin Tower (their
canonical decomp placement, 7/9/12,9), gated on EVENT_RELEASED_THE_BEASTS — the
flag the already-enabled Burned Tower "release the beasts" scene sets. So you wake
them at the Burned Tower, then confront them at Tin Tower. Tin Tower is reachable
(the Ecruteak sage-block is seeded off).

Required a small refactor: LEGENDARY_ENCOUNTERS values can now be a single entry OR
an array, so a map can hold several legendaries. legendariesHere() returns all
un-caught, requirement-met entries on the current map; drawLegendary and
checkLegendaryTrigger iterate/find over it (legendaryHere() kept as the first, for
single-per-map back-compat). With this, all 16 legendaries are catchable.

Test: legendary_test.mjs (30 — the beasts are absent before the release and all
three appear after). No regressions.

entries.title: overworld: the Legendary Hunt — catchable legendaries + key-item gates
entries.body:
Only 3 legendaries were catchable (the Hoenn trio); every other legendary's decomp
encounter uses a StartLegendaryBattle special this port treats as a no-op, so they
despawned without a battle. This makes the marquee legendaries catchable and gates
the endgame ones behind key items / Champion status — unifying roadmap item 2
(key-item puzzles + legendary plot).

Extended LEGENDARY_ENCOUNTERS with the Kanto birds (Articuno/Zapdos/Moltres, in
their lairs, ungated), Mewtwo (Cerulean Cave, requires KANTO Champion), and the
Johto tower duo Ho-Oh (Tin Tower, requires the Rainbow Wing) and Lugia (Whirl
Islands, requires the Silver Wing). Added an optional `requires` predicate honored
in legendaryHere() so a gated legendary is simply absent (not drawn, no trigger) —
never a strand, since all gated legendaries are optional.

Key-item puzzle: becoming the JOHTO Champion grants the Rainbow + Silver Wing
(onTrainerDefeated champion branch), which then summon Ho-Oh and Lugia — a post-game
hunt. All 16 legendary species + their overworld sprites already exist, so they
render and battle for real.

The full multi-map awakening cutscenes (Sootopolis crisis / Sky Pillar) are deferred
(they warp the player + rely on unreliable setmetatile edits); the per-encounter
intro text carries the awakening beat.

Test: legendary_test.mjs (22 — species+sprites resolve, gated legendaries absent
until Champion/wing then present, ungated bird present, Champion grants the wings).
No regressions across all 11 suites (469 assertions).

entries.title: overworld: real Emerald art for the Hoenn gym leaders
entries.body:
The 8 Hoenn gym leaders (+ Wallace/Juan) used generic fallback sprites because the
Emerald sprite set was never imported. Their real overworld sprites already exist
in the on-disk pokeemerald checkout in the game's exact format (48x32/144x32, 4bpp
indexed, frames 0/1/2 = down/up/left), so they're copied verbatim — no conversion —
into a new tracked overworld/people_extra/ dir (not under data/, so it deploys via
the MAIN site rather than the read-only owdata data dir).

trainers.js spritePath() (replacing the generic-only fallback) routes the leader
graphics ids to people_extra/<name>.png and everything else to a generic default;
used in both trainers.js and npcs.js after the specific data/people sprite 404s.

Test: villain_test (47 — Roxanne renders her real 48x32 art from people_extra, not
a generic). No regressions.

entries.title: overworld: make Hoenn playable + the Seafloor Cavern full crawl
entries.body:
Moving the Aqua boss to the deep Seafloor Cavern room uncovered two pre-existing
bugs that made all of Hoenn non-functional:

1. The Emerald map parser omits the `type:"object"` field on object_events (Kanto
   and Johto have it), and npcs.js + isTrainerEvent + claims all required
   `ev.type === 'object'` — so NO Hoenn trainer or NPC ever spawned. Gym leaders
   included, which meant Hoenn gyms were unbeatable and the region uncompletable.
   Fix: treat a missing type as object (object_events are always objects).

2. The Emerald sprite set was never imported, so all 8 Hoenn gym leaders have no
   people/*.png and silently failed to spawn even once they were claimed. Fix: a
   code-level SPRITE_FALLBACK (gfx_map.json is read-only owdata) maps the leaders
   to gender-appropriate generics, with a universal spriteFor() fallback used in
   both trainers.js and npcs.js so a missing sprite can never hide a battleable NPC.

Now Hoenn routes are populated, gym leaders spawn and battle (Roxanne verified),
and the villain grunts populate the dungeons.

Seafloor Cavern full crawl (the original task): the Archie confrontation moves to
Room 9 (the Kyogre awakening) with grunts + Shelly populating the cavern. The Room
8 Strength/Rock-Smash boulder maze is the faithful, solvable vanilla layout AND
items.js rebuilds field objects per visit, so the boulders reset on room re-entry
— the maze can never permanently strand, and the player has Strength/Rock Smash by
7 badges.

Test: villain_test (46 — Seafloor grunts spawn at the deep boss room, a Hoenn gym
leader spawns + resolves a team, a Hoenn route is populated). Strand-safe:
quest_reach (107) covers Room 9 + cavern reachability. No regressions across the
other suites (446 assertions total).

entries.title: overworld: populate the villain dungeons — real crawls
entries.body:
The hideouts were empty (every grunt is a flag-hidden object_event skipped by
trainers.js). Now the grunts spawn while their beat is active and the boss moves
to the deep floor, so the villain fights are real dungeon crawls.

trainers.js: a spawnFlagged hook un-hides flagged grunt events (the flag-skip at
:105 becomes conditional); spawned ones are marked t.villain. Grunts route through
the existing sight -> buildBattle -> markDefeated pipeline with real teams
(Kanto/Hoenn rosters, Johto via classPools). occupied() now skips defeated so a
beaten grunt can't wall a corridor (checkSight already skipped them).

quest.js: each VILLAIN_BEATS beat gains `maps` (grunt-spawn floors) and its `at`
moves to the deep boss floor (RocketHideout_B4F, SilphCo_11F, SlowpokeWellB2F,
TeamRocketBaseB3F, AquaHideout_B2F). The boss fires on ENTERING that floor, so it
never depends on reaching a specific tile. Hoenn Seafloor stays a single-room
confrontation (its Room 9 is boulder-maze-gated — kept safe so the League gate
can't strand). isDungeonFloor(region,map) drives the spawn hook.

main.js: sets trainers.spawnFlagged; re-loads trainers when a beat completes so
grunts vanish; and SILPH DOOR-FIX — my setMetatile now let SilphCo's OnLoad erect
the Card-Key door barriers (walling the Giovanni ascent), so runMapTransition skips
/^SilphCo_\d/ (that OnLoad only closes doors; the Elevator is untouched).

Strand-safe: quest_reach asserts every boss + grunt floor is reachable at the
beat's badge level (98 assertions). villain_test (42) proves grunts spawn on the
crawl floor, resolve a real team, don't block when beaten, and SilphCo loads. No
regressions across all 10 suites (433 assertions).

entries.title: overworld: weave the villain arcs into the quest as required gated steps
entries.body:
Team Rocket (Kanto & Johto) and Team Aqua (Hoenn) are now part of the main quest:
boss confrontations that seal a gym or the League until you beat them.

Enabling fact from recon: every villain NPC in the map data is inert — npcs.js:126
and trainers.js:105 skip any object_event with a story flag, so all grunts/execs/
bosses never spawn and the dungeon warps are open; nothing reads the canonical
flags. So the villain layer is entirely code-driven (no decomp scene to collide
with, and the boss battles supply their own teams), mirroring the Fork-B intro
pattern (a code-triggered cutscene + an inline-team battle).

quest.js VILLAIN_BEATS (2 beats/region, inline boss teams — Kanto/Hoenn from
trainer_teams.json, Johto authored since the Crystal constants ship no teams):
  - REQUIRED (gate a gym/League): Silph Co Giovanni -> Sabrina; Slowpoke Well
    Proton -> Bugsy; Mahogany Rocket HQ Ariana -> Pryce; Seafloor Cavern Archie
    -> the League.
  - flavor (ungated, discoverable): Kanto Rocket Hideout, Hoenn Aqua Hideout.
A required beat's objective replaces the gym objective while it gates the next gym;
blocked() adds a villain flag-gate that takes precedence over the badge gate; the
QUEST log interleaves villain rows.

main.js checkVillainTrigger() (in refreshMapContent) fires the boss speech + battle
on entering the beat's entrance floor; a win sets the doneFlag (opening the gated
gym/League) + advances the objective, a loss heals in place (re-enter to retry).
Triggering at the entrance floor keeps it strand-safe (reliably reachable at the
beat's badge level). Dungeon interiors are not populated yet (deferred).

Test: villain_test.mjs (32 — unit beat/objective/gate transitions + every boss
team's species resolves + headless: the ARCHIE confrontation fires, the League is
sealed until the climax, then opens). No regressions across the other 9 suites
(368 assertions).

entries.title: overworld: restore Sootopolis's dive-in so Hoenn can be completed
entries.body:
The web port left SootopolisCity and Underwater_SootopolisCity with zero
connections, so Wallace's gym (Hoenn's 8th) was unreachable and the region
couldn't be finished — surfaced by the quest reachability check.

The rest of the entry chain already exists (Route126 --dive--> Underwater_Route126
--warp--> Underwater_SootopolisCity); only the final hop into the city was missing.
Because the map JSONs are served read-only from the owdata deployment (a
/overworld/data/* redirect), the missing link is restored in CODE rather than data:

  - new overworld/divelinks.js exports EXTRA_DIVE: the underwater room EMERGES up
    into the Sootopolis lake, and the city DIVES back down;
  - main.js diveConn() merges a map's own dive/emerge connections with EXTRA_DIVE,
    and diveTo() honors an explicit landing (the twins differ in size, 20x10 vs
    60x60) by snapping to the nearest surfable water (emerge) or walkable seabed
    (dive) and setting the surf state from the tile it actually lands on;
  - the DIVE field move uses diveConn so it's recognized in both maps.

DIVE is badge-gated (Hoenn needs 7 badges), so this naturally gates Sootopolis
behind gym 7 — consistent with the quest corridor. The reachability graph mirrors
the restored edge, so quest_reach now confirms Sootopolis is reachable at 7 badges
(no more data-gap warning).

Test: dive_test.mjs (9 — emerge lands on valid surfable water, the gym is present
and enterable, diving back down lands on walkable seabed). No regressions across
boot/badges/progression/gymstory/intro/plot/quest (359 assertions).

entries.title: overworld: linear main-quest spine + strict-corridor area gating (all 3 regions)
entries.body:
Turn the guided-but-open overworld into a linear, gym-by-gym journey with an
on-screen objective and strict area gating, for Kanto/Johto/Hoenn.

New module overworld/quest.js (modeled on badges.js): per-region ordered GYMS
table drives both the objective text and a gym-door gate. Stage is DERIVED from
the badge count + intro/champion state (no new persistence, can't desync):
INTRO -> gym 0..7 -> LEAGUE (8 badges) -> DONE (champion).

Strict corridor gating (the user chose the strict-corridor style): a GATED_MAPS
table (town/route boundaries -> required badges) merged with auto gym-door gates
(gym k needs k badges, so gyms can't be beaten out of order even where the town
is reachable early — Viridian/Saffron/Olivine/Petalburg). Wired at the two
player.onArrive choke points (connection cross + warp). STRAND-PROOF: a move is
only blocked when it advances DEEPER than where you stand AND deeper than your
badges — retreating/lateral is never blocked, so an old save left mid-region can
always walk back to a gym.

Verified strand-free by a BFS reachability check (quest_reach.mjs) over the real
connection+warp graph: from each start, every gym town is reachable at exactly
its badge index and reachability only grows with badges. (Sootopolis is flagged
as a pre-existing data gap — its dive-in was never wired in the port, so Wallace's
gym is currently unreachable; noted for a later fix.)

Objective UI: a persistent #objective HUD line (desktop), a QUEST entry in the
Start menu (a done/current/locked quest log), and an OBJECTIVE row on the Trainer
Card. refreshObjective() fires on map load, badge earned, champion, and intro end.

Deferred to later passes (explicitly out of scope now): weaving the villain arcs
into the sequence as gated steps, and the cross-region portals + badge-thirds
layer (the region-parallel 8-gym shape is built to accept it).

Tests: quest_test.mjs (71 — unit stage/objective/gate/log for all regions + the
retreat rule + headless wiring) and quest_reach.mjs (74 — reachability/no-strand).
No regressions: boot 5, badges 106, progression 15, gymstory 15, intro 59, plot 13.

entries.title: overworld: turn on the deeper plot cutscenes (audited-safe set) + cutscene safety net
entries.body:
Selectively re-enable the ported plot cutscenes that STORY_SEED was suppressing.
Audited every rested scene var per region and removed the SAFE ones from the seed
so their scene-0 coord_events cold-fire, while keeping the dangerous ones rested.

Enabled (dialogue/battle/flavor only — no player-warp, no tile edits, one-shot):
  Hoenn — Route 110 & 119 rival ambushes, Petalburg Woods Aqua grunt, Scott's
  cameo, Steven on Route 118, the Route 121 Aqua move-out, Wally's Victory Road
  battle (all self-advance their state var, so they play once).
  Johto — Mom's greeting, the Route 27 fisher, the Burned Tower legendary-beasts
  awakening, the Team Rocket HQ security cameras + floor traps -> grunt battles
  (self-EVENT-guarded), the B2F Lance heal, the Goldenrod Underground + Victory
  Road rival ambushes, and the Indigo Plateau rival.

Kept seeded (would strand/corrupt a free-roam save): the Oldale/Petalburg blocks,
Meteor Falls / Mt Pyre cross-map flag flips + key item, the Seafloor Cavern warp,
the Sky Pillar Rayquaza-hide, the New Bark block, every force-move-the-player gate
(Route 32, Mahogany, Olivine, Sprout Tower, Wise Trio, Magnet Train), the ship-
boarding warps, the Radio Tower key-item hand-off, and the Ecruteak stair-block.

One-shot guard (PLOT_ONESHOT + magepunk_plot_fired in checkCoordTrigger): the
enabled scenes that don't self-advance fire once then suppress; a scene's multiple
trigger tiles share one key (e.g. VictoryRoadRivalLeft/Right) so it can't replay.

Safety net (prereq for enabling any plot cutscene):
  - every map loader (warpTo/moveToMap/crossConnection/flyTo/diveTo/backWarp)
    guarded so a throwing world.load can't strand loading=true (a failed load
    leaves the player on the valid old map — this.current only updates on success);
  - two tick watchdogs: a stuck load (>12s) force-clears; a cutscene that blocks
    with no dialog/battle/menu (>30s) force-stops;
  - the ported plot triggers are try/catch-guarded so a bad story script can't
    break map entry or stepping onto a tile.

Test: overworld/tests/plot_test.mjs (13 headless — seed correctness both regions,
a safe scene fires, an unsafe scene stays suppressed, the one-shot shared-group
guard). No regressions: boot 5, badges 106, progression 15, gymstory 15, intro 59.

entries.title: overworld: Fork B authentic campaign open (region pick → no starter → lab pick → rival)
entries.body:
A brand-new game no longer hands you a starter up front. Fresh save now opens a
REGION picker (no starter grid); you begin with NO Pokemon, hear the professor's
welcome, walk to the lab where a code-triggered cutscene runs the professor
greeting + an ON-SCREEN starter pick, then the rival grabs the type-advantaged
starter and battles you before the Pokedex handoff.

Hand-authored in main.js (NEW_GAME_INTRO table for Kanto/Johto/Hoenn) using
supported cutscene ops rather than decomp replay — the transpiled intro scripts
can't grant a starter (Johto's givepoke was dropped, Hoenn's is buried in a
native ChooseStarter special) and the interpreter has no multichoice op. The
ported plot stays seeded off (STORY_SEED); this intro is the genuine open,
code-driven (lab-entry trigger + custom picker) so it never depends on fragile
decomp NPC-walk choreography.

Robustness: a partyless player is bounced back from town-edge connections
(player.onArrive) so there's no wild-route softlock, and world.setMetatile is now
implemented (engine.js repaints one cell into the cached canvases) + wired to
cutsceneCtx, unblocking future passage-opening plot scenes.

Test: overworld/tests/intro_test.mjs (22 headless — Kanto path + setMetatile).
No regressions: boot 5, badges 106, progression 15, gymstory 15.

entries.title: overworld: extend authentic scripted battles to ALL trainers
entries.body:
Broadens the Gym-Leader routing to every ordinary trainer: engaging (or being
spotted by) a trainer now plays their ported EventScript — the pre-battle taunt,
the battle, and the post-battle line — instead of a bare battle. Their scripts
are trivially safe (trainerbattle / msg / end, all interpreter-handled; no warps
or tile edits), verified across Pewter Gym, Routes 3/4, and Viridian Forest.

- onEngage runs runScriptLabel for any trainer whose script body is loaded,
  EXCEPT the Elite Four / Champion (kept on the gated plain-battle path — their
  decomp scripts warp room-to-room and roll credits, a later pass). Falls back to
  the plain battle if no script body is present.
- Ordinary trainers award no badge (scriptInfo returns null); only Gym Leaders
  do, silently via the scripted-battle hook. Regression-guarded in the test.

Test: gymstory_test.mjs now 15 assertions (adds: an ordinary trainer routes to
his script, awards no badge, renders clean). progression 15/15, boot 5/5.

entries.title: overworld: turn the story on for Gym Leaders (authentic scripted battles)
entries.body:
Gym Leaders battled via the bare talk-to path, skipping their entire ported
EventScript — the leader's speech, the badge/TM ceremony, the NPC state changes.
This routes a Gym Leader engagement through its real decomp script (run by the
existing cutscene interpreter), so beating Brock now plays: his rock-hard
challenge → the battle → "I confer on you the BOULDERBADGE" → the TM39 gift →
post-battle dialogue, exactly as ported.

- main.js onEngage: if the engaged trainer is a Gym Leader and its script body
  is loaded, run it via runScriptLabel (leader speech + trainerbattle op +
  ceremony) instead of a plain battle. Falls back to the plain battle + synthetic
  toast if the script isn't present.
- The badge is still recorded through the scripted-battle victory hook, now with
  a { silent: true } flag so it does NOT double the authentic speech (which
  already announces the badge). The non-scripted path keeps its toast.
- events.js resolveText: broaden control-code stripping to drop arg'd tokens like
  {PAUSE 0x56} / {PLAY_BGM ...} (the old /[A-Z_0-9]+/ missed them), and normalize
  é → e so ported strings read POKeMON, matching the game's font convention.
  This cleans ALL scripted dialogue, not just gyms.

Elite Four / Champion stay on the gated bare-battle + crown path for now (their
decomp scripts warp room-to-room and roll credits — a later, separate pass), as
do the map/plot coord-event cutscenes (still suppressed by STORY_SEED; they need
setMetatile + per-scene verification).

Test: overworld/tests/gymstory_test.mjs — 12 headless assertions (Brock's script
loads, engaging him opens the authentic speech, no leaked {codes}, é normalized,
closing the speech starts the Leader battle, scripted win records the badge
silently, non-scripted path still toasts). badges 106/106, progression 15/15,
boot_smoke 5/5 — no regressions.

entries.title: overworld: add the progression spine (badges → Elite Four → Champion) + HM area gating
entries.body:
The overworld was a free-roam sandbox: Gym Leaders, the Elite Four, and
Champions all existed as battleable NPCs but beating one did nothing, and every
HM was usable from turn one. This adds the connective tissue that makes it a
game with a goal to climb toward — region-agnostic, working across Kanto, Johto,
and Hoenn. (Narrative cutscenes are a deferred follow-up; this is the spine.)

New overworld/badges.js:
- Per-region ordered badge tables (Kanto/Johto/Hoenn, 8 each).
- Gym-leader battle-script → badge map (FireRed/Emerald EventScript_* +
  pokecrystal *Script; both leader variants + JohKanto Kanto gyms included).
- Elite Four/Champion script → {region, role} map.
- HM → required-badge-count gate per region, in canonical badge order
  (FRLG flash/cut/fly/strength/surf = 1..5; RSE cut..waterfall = 1..8;
  GSC flash/cut/strength/surf/fly = 1..5, waterfall = 8).
- Persistence via safestore (device-local, node-safe), with a champion crown.

Wired into main.js:
- A Gym Leader victory awards that region's badge with a toast (both the
  talk-to and cutscene-script battle paths).
- The Elite Four / Champion refuse to battle until you hold all 8 region
  badges; beating the Champion crowns you and rolls a Hall of Fame message.
- HM field moves are badge-gated out of battle (still usable in battle);
  can't strand a player — walking back to land auto-dismounts Surf, and
  canonical order grants each HM's badge before it's needed.
- The trainer card shows a badges count, an 8-pip badge case, and a
  CHAMPION mark.

Tests (dev-machine; not in run-all.mjs):
- overworld/tests/badges_test.mjs — 106 pure-node unit assertions (mappings,
  earn/count, per-region HM thresholds, League math, champion, persistence).
- overworld/tests/progression_test.mjs — 15 headless-Chrome assertions driving
  the real main.js wiring (badge award, League gate open/closed, HM gate
  blocked→allowed, Champion crown, trainer-card render). boot_smoke still 5/5.

entries.title: per-mode achievements for Dungeon/Heist/Tombs/Duels/Arena
entries.body:
13 new achievements on the profile, specific to each run mode (the old ones only
counted total runs/wins across all modes):
- Dungeon: Treasure Hunter (clear 1), Dungeon Conqueror (clear 5)
- Heist: Cracked the Vault (complete 1), Master Thief (clear 1), Kingpin (clear 5)
- Tombs: Tomb Raider (complete 1), Plague Ender (clear a chapter)
- Duels: Duelist (complete 1), Duels Champion (win a run / 12 wins)
- Arena: Arena Drafter (complete 1), Arena Regular (complete 10), Arena Ace (win
  7+ in one run), Flawless Arena (go 12-0)

Server: run-reward now takes a `mode` and increments per-mode counters in
user.stats.modes[mode].{runs,wins}; publicState surfaces arenaBest so the Arena
Ace/Flawless achievements read from your best run. Client: mpRunReward derives the
mode from the run-mode flags (runModeName) and passes it — no call-site changes.
profile/index.html computes m.<mode> + m.arenaBestWins from state and adds the
achievements. Existing generic run/win achievements kept (no un-earning).

Tests: relay_harness (59 — run-reward tracks per-mode counters via the real handler
across dungeon/heist/arena, and publicState carries arenaBest). Profile render
verified headless (33 achievements; the right ones unlock from per-mode stats).
Full suite 202/202.

entries.title: live deck analytics panel in the deck builder
entries.body:
The deck footer now shows a live mana-curve histogram (costs 0–7+) plus average
cost and a type + rarity breakdown, updating as you add/remove cards. Helps a
player see at a glance whether a deck is top-heavy or unfocused. Hidden when the
working deck is empty. Client-only, computed in updateCounts (renderDeckStats).

Test: deck_codes_smoke +2 (19 — after loading a 40-card starter the panel shows an
8-bucket curve summing to 40, plus avg cost + type + rarity lines). Full suite
202/202.

entries.title: Arena leaderboard — global rankings of best runs
entries.body:
Finishing an Arena run now submits your record; the server keeps your BEST run
(most wins, fewest losses as the tiebreak) and mirrors it into a single capped
global board. A "🏆 Leaderboard" overlay on the run-over/flawless screens (and the
resume screen) shows the top 50 runs, highlights you, and shows your best + rank.

Server (mp.mjs): arena-score (token-gated, rate-limited, wins clamped 0-12 /
losses 0-3) updates user.arenaBest + arena:board (top 100, sorted wins-desc then
losses-asc then earliest-when); arena-leaderboard returns the top 50 + your rank.
pubprofile now surfaces arenaBest too.

Client (game.js): submitArenaScore() on both arena end screens; showArenaLeaderboard()
overlay (own stacking element above the run overlay).

Tests: server_arena_test (16, in run-all — endpoint shape + the best-comparison and
board-sort logic); relay_harness (57 — a worse run doesn't replace your best, a 12-0
ranks #1, ordering + your rank via the REAL handler); arena_smoke (9 — the overlay
renders the top runs, highlights you, shows your rank). Full suite 202/202.

entries.title: new accounts start with the starter-deck cards, not the whole pool
entries.body:
A new account no longer starts with 2x every common + 1x every uncommon (thousands
of cards). It now starts with a curated, bounded set: every card used by a per-class
starter deck (starter-decks.json) OR a dungeon/heist/tombs run starter deck —
367 cards, 2 each (1 legendary). So a new player owns exactly what they need to play
any starter template or run deck, and packs are how they grow from there.

- tools/gen_starter_decks.mjs also writes battlecards/starter-collection.js
  (STARTING_COLLECTION = the union, generated from starter-decks.json + dungeon.js
  STARTER_DECKS).
- collection.js getCollection() (local mode) grants STARTING_COLLECTION instead of
  the common/uncommon pool. Never removes — existing local collections keep their
  cards, new ones get the curated set.
- server/mp.mjs startingCollection() = STARTING_COLLECTION + the 3 pre-saved PvP
  starter slots' cards. A startersV4 baseline grants it (max, additive) to existing
  accounts so they can load + Save the templates too. (Imports the .js module, not a
  cross-dir JSON, so the relay harness's same-dir JSON patcher stays valid.)

Tests: starter_decks_test (60 — validated against the REAL STARTING_COLLECTION now,
+ it's bounded <1000, + it owns every starter-deck AND every run-deck card); relay
harness 52/52 (registration path exercises the new startingCollection, 0 desyncs);
deck smoke 17/17 (local getCollection). Full suite 201/201.

Regenerate after card/deck changes: node tools/gen_starter_decks.mjs

entries.title: starter decks — one-click ready-to-play templates per class
entries.body:
New players who bounce off building a 40-card deck from scratch can now load a
ready-made starter deck from the deck builder's "Start from a template" section.

- tools/gen_starter_decks.mjs generates one legal, curve-aware 40-card deck per
  class (18 total) into battlecards/starter-decks.json, built ONLY from cards a
  fresh account already owns (2x each common/basic, 1x each uncommon per
  collection.js getCollection) — so every starter loads → Saves → plays with no
  missing cards. Deterministic (sorted picks), midrange curve.
- deck.js: fetches starter-decks.json and renders a "Start from a template" list
  in the My Decks view; clicking loads the deck into the editor as an unsaved deck
  to review + Save (mirrors loadDeckFromCode). start.html tile mentions it.

Tests: starter_decks_test.mjs (57, in run-all — every starter is a legal 40-card
deck a NEW account owns, validated against the REAL collection.js validateDeck +
copy limits, plus a codec round-trip for the ?deck= path); deck_codes_smoke +2
(the template section renders + clicking loads a full 40-card deck). Full suite
201/201.

(Also made the pre-existing slot-share smoke assertion deterministic — headless
clipboard.writeText can hang; fire the handler in-page so it reliably falls back
to the prompt whose default is the ?deck= link.)

entries.title: card-grid keyboard navigation (viewer + deck builder)
entries.body:
The card-grid tiles were clickable <div>s with no keyboard path — the last
deferred item from the site health pass. Now each tile is role="button"
tabindex="0" with an aria-label, and Enter/Space mirrors the mouse click:
- viewer.js: opens the card detail (zoom).
- deck.js: opens the card page (which has the Add button) — a complete keyboard
  path to adding cards; pointer drag-to-deck is untouched.
- deck.js loadout picker tiles: Enter/Space selects the commander/companion.
Added a visible `.tile:focus-visible` ring on both pages so keyboard focus is
clear on the image tiles.

The deck.js change deliberately leaves the drag-and-drop (draggable + dragstart /
touch long-press) intact — the a11y attributes and keydown are additive.

Tests: deck_codes_smoke +3 (15 — a tile is a keyboard button with role/tabindex/
aria-label, and Enter on a focused tile opens the card detail). Viewer verified
headless (tiles focusable, Enter opens zoom, no errors). Full suite 200/200.

entries.title: Site health pass: SEO/meta, security headers, perf, accessibility
entries.body:
Findings from a 3-dimension audit (SEO, a11y, performance), fixes applied. Broken
links audited: clean (no dead links).

SEO / meta:
- Add canonical URLs to all indexable pages (0 had one; Pages serves www+apex+
  *.pages.dev, so this is the top site-wide fix).
- Add description + OG/Twitter to deck/packs/viewer/replays (had none).
- Fix root title/og:title (bare "Magepunk" → "Magepunk — Games, Cards & Worlds").
- Fix viewer's mislabeled "Collection" title → "Card Gallery" (collided with the
  real /collection/ page).
- Add lang="en" to deck/packs/viewer (were bare <html>).
- Add favicons to login/profile (were 404ing /favicon.ico); noindex on login+profile.

Performance:
- collection/ was missing the card-art preconnect its siblings all have (it's the
  most art-heavy page) — added, plus a cdn.jsdelivr.net preconnect on all four
  card-render pages (three.js + Mana font).
- Kill the theme flash (FOUC): move the mp-theme restore into a blocking <head>
  script on index/start/replays (was at end of <body>).

Security headers (_headers): add X-Frame-Options: DENY (site uses no iframes —
protects the login form from clickjacking), Strict-Transport-Security, and a
Permissions-Policy locking down camera/mic/geolocation.

Accessibility:
- aria-labels on icon-only buttons (viewer ◀▶✕, deck ✕‹›) + the filter selects.
- prefers-reduced-motion guards for viewer's infinite gemspin + deck transitions.
- Darken below-AA muted grays on collection/profile (#76819c/#98a2bd on the light
  bg → #565f7a/#697396).
- Real focus-visible ring on the login inputs (was outline:none).
- deck.html brand → <h1> (page had no h1); start.html live-name + topbar DM row
  made keyboard-operable (role/tabindex/Enter+Space).

Verified: full suite 200/200; deck.html + start.html boot clean headless (12/12,
5/5). Deferred (noted): converting the viewer/deck card-grid <div> tiles to
keyboard-operable buttons (touches drag-and-drop — higher risk).

entries.title: instant game-over for spectators (0s, not ~20s)
entries.body:
Spectators previously learned a watched game ended only via cardstate STALENESS —
after the publisher went quiet, ~20s later the snapshot lapsed and the client
raised GAME OVER. Now the publisher stamps over/winner on the final board so
spectators see the result the moment it happens.

- publish-cardstate stores over/winner from the client; startPublishLoop passes
  state.over/state.winner (the final quiet-publish carries over:true).
- card-publish mirrors over/winner into the cardstate payload too, so duel
  spectators on the cardstate channel also get it instantly.
- The cardstate delta (unchanged) branch carries over/winner as well, so a
  spectator polling at the same seq isn't left waiting.
- startSpectate: showSpectateOver(winner) raises GAME OVER immediately (with the
  winner's class/name, or "draw"), on both the full-ingest and unchanged paths;
  it also unmounts chat. The ~20s staleness path remains as a fallback (publisher
  crash / no over signal) and for the joined-an-already-ended-game case.

Tests: server_spectators_test (33 — over/winner stored in cardstate + card-publish
+ the unchanged delta); spectate_smoke (20 — the spectator sees GAME OVER with the
winner instantly from the over flag, not staleness); relay_harness (52, unchanged —
duel over/winner still flows, zero desyncs). Full suite 200/200.

entries.title: fix the two remaining low audit items (post-game cleanup)
entries.body:
1. Publisher goes quiet after game-over. startPublishLoop kept republishing the
   final board forever, so a runner lingering on the post-game screen kept
   cardstate fresh and their spectators never got a GAME OVER (until the runner
   navigated away). Now it publishes ONE final board when state.over, then stops
   calling publish-cardstate — cardstate goes stale (~20s) and spectators get the
   overlay (the spectator side was already fixed in the audit pass). The interval
   is kept alive (not cleared) so a restart/rematch resumes broadcasting.

2. Chat poll stopped on spectate game-over. The chat's own 1.5s poll loop kept
   running after the watched game ended. startSpectate now calls Chat.unmount()
   when it raises the GAME OVER overlay.

Tests: replay_smoke (13 — the live-game stub counts publish-cardstate; after
forcing state.over, no further publishes in a 3s window); spectate_smoke (20 —
#mp-chat is gone once the watched game ends). Full suite 200/200.

entries.title: adversarial review pass on spectation — fix 4 real bugs
entries.body:
A focused audit (3 parallel review agents, every finding verified against source)
of the spectation/social system surfaced these, now fixed:

HIGH — card-poll had NO authorization: any logged-in user who knew a match id got
the full board + watcherNames (the id is not a capability). Added the same
participant-OR-friend-of-participant gate card-match uses. (Flagged independently
by two agents; also means SPEC_CAP now can't be bypassed via card-poll.)

MEDIUM — isSpectatorOf let a duel OPPONENT into the spectator-only chat: the
participant-exclusion relied on the runner having a live m: cardstate row, but a
duel GUEST publishes u:<guest> (via startPublishLoop), so a guest's opponent (a
friend) could read spec:<guest>. Now derives co-participation from the CALLER's own
curmatch — robust regardless of host/guest.

MEDIUM — flip-view didn't rebuild panels: switching which player you spectate
changed HUMAN but not foePanelEls / slot geometry (both built relative to HUMAN),
so the board rendered with the wrong/duplicated foe panels. Now rebuilds on flip.

MEDIUM — game-over handling: guarded data.unchanged against a null response, and a
spectator who JOINS an already-ended game now sees a "not live" overlay instead of
polling silently forever (was gated on spectateSeq>=0, never true on join).

Low hardening: chat esc() now escapes quotes (safe in attribute context — not
exploitable since usernames are [a-z0-9_], but correct); chat dedup key includes
the message body (two distinct same-ms messages no longer collide); seen set capped.

Verified clean by the agents (no change): cap overshoot bounded/self-limiting,
heartbeat GC wired, delta-seq no false-unchanged + tail always present, rate limits
2.4-4x headroom, no stuck loops, no watcher-name prefix collisions, pubprofile /
live-friends leak nothing private.

Tests: server_spectators_test (30 — card-poll authz + curmatch-exclusion guards);
relay_harness (52 — a stranger is refused card-poll, a duel opponent can't read the
spec chat, a non-participant friend still can); spectate_smoke (19 — flip rebuilds
the foe set, a spectator sees GAME OVER when the watched game ends). Full 200/200.

entries.title: harden the spectate poll — rate limit + adaptive backoff
entries.body:
The spectator/duel-guest polls (cardstate, card-poll) were the only live actions
with NO rate limit, so a runaway/buggy client could hammer them unbounded. Added
generous per-user ceilings to RATE_LIMITS (cardstate 40/10s ≈ 4/s vs the ~1/s
legit poll; card-poll 80/10s ≈ 8/s vs ~3/s during a turn) — well above real
clients, only tripping a hammering one (429 "slow down").

Client (spectator): adaptive backoff — poll ~1s while the board is changing,
relax to 2.5s after 3 consecutive unchanged (delta) polls, snap back to 1s on any
update; the loop also STOPS once the game-over overlay shows (no more polling a
dead game). A rate-limit/transient error response is now skipped (not mistaken for
game-over). The duel guest was already adaptive (300/850ms by turn) and already
tolerates an error response.

Tests: server_spectators_test (26 — cardstate + card-poll are rate-limited);
relay_harness (48 — hammering cardstate trips the 429, still zero desyncs).
Full suite 200/200.

entries.title: card-poll delta too (duel guests skip unchanged snapshots)
entries.body:
Same delta as cardstate, now on the duel relay: the guest sends seq: duel.seq in
its card-poll, and the server returns a tiny {unchanged:true, seq, watchers,
watcherNames, ...tail} when the seq matches — no snapshot re-sent. The over/winner
tail is ALWAYS included so abandonment is still detected on an unchanged poll. The
guest needed no logic change beyond sending its seq: its ingest already gates on
data.snapshot, so an unchanged response is skipped transparently. The one-shot
resume fetch keeps no seq (still gets the full board). Debug note gains an
"unchanged" state.

Tests: server_spectators_test (25 — card-poll delta guard, keeps ...tail);
relay_harness (47 — card-poll same seq → unchanged with the over tail intact,
stale seq → full; live browser guests now delta-poll with zero desyncs). Full
suite 200/200.

entries.title: spectator delta updates — skip re-sending an unchanged snapshot
entries.body:
Spectators poll cardstate every 1s, but the board changes far less often — and
every poll was re-downloading the entire (up-to-2MB FFA) snapshot. Now the
spectator sends its last-seen seq; if the server's seq matches, it returns a tiny
{unchanged:true, seq, watchers, watcherNames} ack instead of the snapshot. That
cuts the dominant spectator bandwidth/D1-read cost by roughly the fraction of
polls where nothing changed (usually most of them).

Client startSpectate sends seq: spectateSeq and, on an unchanged ack, just
refreshes the watcher badge and skips the re-ingest. Bonus: the watcher count is
now recomputed fresh on every poll (the cap already scanned the heartbeats), so it
updates every second instead of only on publish — free.

Tests: server_spectators_test (24 — delta source guard); relay_harness (45 —
same seq → unchanged ack with no snapshot; stale seq → full snapshot);
spectate_smoke (17 — the client polls with its seq and gets an unchanged ack,
board persists). Full suite 200/200.

entries.title: cap spectators at 10 per game (server-enforced)
entries.body:
A game now holds at most SPEC_CAP=10 concurrent spectators, enforced server-side
in the cardstate poll: a NEW viewer is turned away with {full:true, max:10} (403)
once the game is at the cap, while someone already watching (a fresh heartbeat) is
never dropped. The cap is per-GAME — gameWatchers() aggregates across a duel's
participants (a spectator may watch the host or a guest) and excludes the players
themselves, so two duel players can't each admit 10.

listWatchers now returns the full list (so the cap counts the true total);
display sites (publish-cardstate / card-publish) slice to SPEC_CAP. Client: a
turned-away spectator sees a "SPECTATOR SLOTS FULL — waiting for a spot" overlay
and keeps polling, auto-joining when a stale watcher (12s window) frees a slot.

Tests: server_spectators_test (23 — SPEC_CAP/gameWatchers/full-reject guards);
relay_harness (43 — seed 10 heartbeats: the 11th is turned away, admitted when a
slot frees, and an already-watching viewer is never dropped even over the cap);
spectate_smoke (16 — a full response shows the waiting overlay). Full suite 200/200.

entries.title: players see who's watching their own game (incl. duel guests)
entries.body:
The runner/duel-host already saw the "👁 N watching: names" badge (their publish
returns watcherNames). Two gaps closed for duels:

- The GUEST saw nothing: spectators watch the host (spec:<host>), but the guest
  counted its own empty spec:<guest>. Now the guest shows the badge from its
  card-poll data (data.watchers/watcherNames), and startPublishLoop skips the
  badge during a duel so it doesn't overwrite it with the guest's own count.
- card-publish now AGGREGATES watchers across ALL participants (a spectator may
  watch the host OR a guest), so both players see everyone watching the game —
  and EXCLUDES participants (a player isn't a watcher of their own game).

Tests: server_spectators_test (20 — aggregation source guards); relay_harness
(40 — a duel publish lists a non-participant spectator across participants and
does NOT list the players themselves; still zero desyncs). Full suite 200/200.

entries.title: click a watcher or chat name to see their profile
entries.body:
New profile.js openProfile(username): a popup showing a player's online status +
current activity, public stats (wins/runs/packs/unique cards/decks), member-since,
and an Add-friend button (or "Already friends"/you). Fetches a new server
pubprofile action — a SAFE public subset of ANY player that deliberately omits
the collection contents, decks, packs, friends list, and credentials (those stay
in the owner's publicState).

Clickable names in two places: the "👁 N watching" pill (each watcher name is a
link; self shows as "you" but opens the real profile) and chat author names
(.mc-who gets data-user + pointer-events:auto so it's clickable through the
otherwise click-through chat log; a delegated listener opens the profile). Covers
"click a watcher OR a player's name" — players appear as chat authors.

Tests: relay_harness (38 — pubprofile returns safe stats + isFriend, does NOT
leak collection/decks/friends/packs/credentials, unknown user → error);
spectate_smoke (15 — stubbed pubprofile: clicking a watcher name opens the popup
with name+stats+Add-friend, and chat author names carry data-user). Full suite
200/200 (import lint validates the new profile.js graph).

entries.title: show WHO is watching, not just the count
entries.body:
The watcher heartbeat keys are already spec:<runner>:<viewer>, so the viewer
names were there — now they're surfaced. Server: countWatchers → listWatchers
(returns the viewer names, capped at 20); publish-cardstate + card-publish store
+ return watcherNames alongside the count. Client: the "👁 N watching" pill now
lists up to 3 names inline (+K for the rest, full list on hover) — the runner
sees who's watching them, and each spectator sees the watcher list (their own
name shown as "you").

Tests: server_spectators_test (19 — retargeted to listWatchers: names for
fresh/stale/distinct-runner/re-poll); relay_harness (35 — the runner's publish
returns both spectator names, a spectator sees the other by name); spectate_smoke
(13 — dynamic cardstate stub: spectator sees ≥1 self-count first, then the named
watcher list with self as "you"). Full suite 200/200.

entries.title: spectators reliably see the watcher count (≥1, themselves)
entries.body:
The spectator badge was already wired (startSpectate showed data.watchers), but a
fresh/lone spectator saw it HIDDEN until the runner's next publish counted them —
which for duels lags until the host next acts. A watching spectator is always at
least one watcher (themselves), so the spectator badge now shows
Math.max(1, data.watchers) — visible immediately, then converging to the true
count as the runner republishes. The runner's own badge still shows the raw count.

Test: spectate_smoke now sends watchers:0 (the not-yet-counted moment) and asserts
the spectator STILL sees "👁 1 watching" (12). Full suite 200/200.

entries.title: spectators get private emotes + a spectator-only chat channel
entries.body:
Refines the read-only spectator: they can now react and chat, but scoped so the
players never see it.

- Private emotes. A spectator's emote clicks render locally-only (a 👁-tagged
  reaction row) and are never sent — chat.js reactLocal() instead of posting, and
  the server also rejects any emote on a spec: room (defense in depth).
- Spectator-only chat. chat.js gains a dual-room spectator mode: it reads the
  players' room (still read-only) AND reads+writes a spec:<runner> room, merging
  both feeds with spectator messages tagged. Spectator text posts only to
  spec:<runner>. Server: a new isSpectatorOf(X) — a friend of X who is NOT X and
  NOT a co-participant in X's live game — gates spec: rooms in canChat + canPost,
  so other spectators see the chat but the players (and a dueling friend) can't.

Tests: server_spectators_test +4 (19 — isSpectatorOf + spec-room routing + emote
rejection guards); relay_harness (35 — real handler: spectator can't post in the
players' room but CAN post text to spec:, its emote is rejected, another
spectator sees it, the player cannot); spectate_smoke (11 — the chat has input +
emotes, an emote shows a private local row and is NOT sent, text posts to
spec:friendx never the players' room). Full suite 200/200.

entries.title: spectators are read-only in chat + can switch player view
entries.body:
Two spectator refinements:

1. Read-only chat. Spectators could post/emote in the game they were watching.
   Now the client mounts their chat with canPost:false (chat.js already hides the
   input + emote buttons), AND the server enforces it: a new stricter canPost()
   allows only room PARTICIPANTS to post (the runner in a u: room; the humans in
   an m: match), so a friend-spectator gets 403 "read-only". chat-get still uses
   the looser canChat, so spectators can still READ the conversation.

2. Switch which player you watch. startSpectate gains a "🔄 Flip view" button
   (per-player in FFA) that cycles HUMAN so any player's slice sits at the
   camera-bottom — you see that player's hand up close. The choice persists across
   snapshot updates. Reuses the same HUMAN-reorient the replay flip uses.

Tests: server_spectators_test +4 (15 — canPost source guards); relay_harness +4
(32 — real handler: a spectator can't post OR emote (403), the runner can, and
the spectator can still read); spectate_smoke.mjs (7, standalone headless — boots
?spectate= against a stubbed cardstate, asserts read-only chat has no input/emote
and Flip view switches HUMAN 0↔1). Full suite 200/200.

entries.title: live spectator count ("👁 N watching")
entries.body:
A viewer heartbeats spec:<runner>:<viewer> each time it polls a friend's
cardstate; the runner's publish (publish-cardstate / card-publish) counts the
heartbeats seen within SPEC_WINDOW_MS and returns the number. Both the runner
(from its publish response) and each spectator (from the cardstate response) show
a small floating "👁 N watching" pill, hidden at zero. Works for solo, all run
modes, and both sides of a live duel; spec: heartbeats GC after 1h.

Tests: server_spectators_test.mjs (11, in run-all — extracts the real
countWatchers, covers fresh/stale/distinct-runner/re-poll counting + source
guards on the heartbeat write, both publish paths returning watchers, and the GC
entry); relay_harness.mjs +2 (28 — real handler: two friends watch a runner and
its next publish reports 2, and a spectator sees the count too). Full suite
200/200.

entries.title: spectate any friend's game from the friends list
entries.body:
The friends list already showed a ● LIVE badge + Watch button (→ ?spectate=),
but two things kept it from working for every game:

1. Wrong game TYPE for most modes. startPublishLoop only reported 'dungeon' or
   'battle', so a friend in Heist/Tombs/Duels/Arena showed as a generic "card
   battle". Now it maps every run mode (+ 'pvp' for duels) and publishes a
   progress label ("Fight 3/8", "5W / 2L") the friends list appends to the
   activity line. Added the missing 'arena' → "an Arena run" to CARD_MODE_LABEL.

2. Duel GUESTS weren't spectatable. The host mirrors its board to cardstate via
   card-publish (already sets card:pvp), but the guest only polls, so a friend of
   the guest saw nothing. The guest now runs the publish loop too, broadcasting
   its view as card:pvp — so either side of a duel is watchable.

Solo, all five run modes, and both sides of a live duel are now spectatable, each
labeled with its real type + progress.

Tests: friends_activity_test.mjs (17, in run-all — extracts friendActivity +
CARD_MODE_LABEL from topbar.js, covers every mode incl. the arena gap, the
region-detail append, pokemon/idle/offline, + source guards on the Watch routing);
relay_harness.mjs +1 (26 — each duel guest broadcasts a spectatable card:pvp
board, still zero desyncs). Full suite 199/199.

entries.title: duel replays — both host and guest record + get replay buttons
entries.body:
Live PvP duels are host-authoritative, so the two sides recorded differently:
- Host already recorded via the engine event loop + finalized in the gameOver
  event; it just needed Watch/Copy buttons on its duel-over overlay.
- Guest never hits the settled-render tail (it ingests the host's snapshots), so
  it now records the authoritative board on each ingest (deduped by digest) and
  finalizes both on the normal data.over path AND in its concede path (a
  conceding guest builds its own #duel-over and stops polling, so it'd otherwise
  never save). The settled tail is gated with !isGuest() so a guest's optimistic
  pumps don't pollute its tape.

Each player gets a local replay of the duel from their own perspective. Watch
opens it (new tab); Copy link uploads for a shareable ?rshare= URL.
finalizeReplay() gained a resultOverride so a conceder records a 'loss' before
the eventual winner is known.

Test: relay_harness.mjs +2 (25) — after a real 3-client duel ends, asserts every
client saved a multiplayer replay (host via game-over, guests via concede) and
the host overlay offers Watch; still zero desyncs + no fatal errors. Full suite
198/198; replay_smoke 12/12.

entries.title: Watch/Share replay buttons on all run-mode result screens
entries.body:
Dungeon, Heist, Tombs, Duels, and Arena now show the ▶ Watch replay + 🔗 Copy
replay link buttons on their per-fight victory/defeat (and loot / run-end)
screens, same as Quick Match. Wired DRY: every run overlay builds the shared
#dungeon-overlay, so the gameOver handler appends addReplayButtons() to it right
after each victory/defeat runs — one line per mode, covering all their sub-screens.

Watch now opens in a NEW TAB (sync window.open keeps the click gesture; the tab
navigates once the saved id resolves) so rewatching a fight never abandons a
run's loot/progress screen.

Test: replay_smoke.mjs +1 — a window.__game._replayButtonLabels() hook renders
addReplayButtons into a real dungeonOverlay and asserts both buttons appear (the
same path every run overlay uses). Full suite 198/198.

entries.title: post-game Watch/Copy-link buttons + shareable replay links
entries.body:
Post-game summary now offers "▶ Watch replay" (opens the just-saved tape) and
"🔗 Copy replay link". Because a tape is far too big for a URL, the link is
server-backed: the tape uploads to a new backend endpoint and the button copies
a short ?rshare= link that plays it on any device — falling back to copying the
paste-able code when logged out. The replays.html per-row share button does the
same (link when possible, code otherwise).

Backend (server/mp.mjs): replay-put (token-gated, rate-limited, size + code-shape
capped) stores a packed tape under replay:<id>; replay-get (PUBLIC, IP
rate-limited) serves it so shared links open even logged-out. Tapes GC after 30
days. Client: replayrec.uploadReplay/fetchSharedReplay; game.js gained a ?rshare=
flag that fetches + plays a shared tape (reusing the same playback path), plus
addReplayButtons() awaiting the finalize promise so the id is ready at click time.

Tests: server_replay_test.mjs (18, in run-all — extracts the real rateLimit,
pins the handler shape: replay-get public / replay-put gated, both validation
regexes, size cap, GC entry, store round-trip); replay_smoke.mjs +1 (a ?rshare=
link fetches via replay-get and boots playback in real WebGL). Full suite
198/198.

entries.title: game replays — record every game, rewatch frame by frame
entries.body:
Record a tape of game-state snapshots during play and rewatch it in the real 3D
board. We store the ACTUAL states that happened (one frame per changed board,
deduped by stateDigest), NOT a seed+action log — so replays are faithful for
every mode (solo/dungeon/heist/tombs/duels/arena/multiplayer) with zero
dependence on RNG determinism.

- replayrec.js: capture → freeze → toSnapshot → gzip (codec.packString) → a
  quota-guarded localStorage ring buffer (10 recent games). listReplays/getReplay
  /deleteReplay/clearReplays + exportCode/importCode for sharing.
- game.js: records at the settled-render tail (nextEvent's empty-queue branch)
  and finalizes on the gameOver event. Playback (?replay=<id>) reuses the spectate
  ingest pattern — state = E.fromSnapshot(snap, cardsById); updateHud(); the
  always-running animate() loop redraws the 3D board — with input gated off via a
  new replayMode (OR'd into the existing spectateMode guards). Control bar:
  first/prev/play-pause/next/last, scrub slider, speed (0.5-4x), flip-perspective
  (watch from either side), keyboard ←/→/space.
- replays.html/js: list recent games (mode, matchup, result, when), Watch/Delete/
  Copy-code, and Import a pasted replay code. Replays tile added to start.html.
- codec.js: generic packString/unpackString (gzip+base64url) for large blobs.

Tests: codec_test +5 (pack/unpack round-trip); replayrec_test (9 — the whole
pipeline: every captured frame restores to its EXACT state, digest-matched);
replay_smoke.mjs (10, standalone headless — records a tape in node, injects it,
boots index.html?replay= in real WebGL, asserts load/step/scrub/flip + no input
leakage, and that a live game starts recording). Full suite 197/197.

entries.title: share a saved deck straight from the My Decks list
entries.body:
Each saved deck row gets a 🔗 button that copies its ?deck= share link without
opening the deck first (stopPropagation so it doesn't also enter the editor;
clipboard write with a prompt fallback). shareSlot() reuses encodeDeck +
shareUrlFor, so list-sharing and in-editor "Copy Link" produce the same link.

deck_codes_smoke.mjs (12): seeds a saved deck, opens the My Decks list, asserts
the 🔗 button exists, that clicking it does NOT open the editor, and that it
produces a real ?deck= link (accepts the flash or the prompt-fallback default,
since headless clipboard writes are unreliable). Desktop viewport so slot
controls are hit-testable. Full suite 196/196.

entries.title: shareable ?deck= deck links (deep-link into the builder)
entries.body:
A deck is now shareable three ways off the same codec.js code: "🔗 Copy Link"
copies deck.html?deck=<code>, "📋 Copy Code" copies the bare code, and "📥
Import" accepts either a raw code or a pasted ?deck= link (codeFromInput pulls
the code out). Opening a ?deck= link deep-links straight into the builder on that
deck as an unsaved "Imported deck" to review + Save; the param is then stripped
from the URL (clean refresh state), and a bad/stale link falls back to a fresh
blank deck instead of crashing. Import logic refactored into a shared
loadDeckFromCode() used by both the Import button and the boot-time link handler.
The code is base64url + '.', all URL-safe, so no query encoding is needed.

deck_codes_smoke.mjs extended (9): the three buttons exist, a ?deck= link opens
the builder on the shared class as "Imported deck" with the param stripped, and a
garbage link falls back cleanly with no new errors. Full suite 196/196.

entries.title: shareable deck codes (Copy/Import in the deck builder)
entries.body:
Encode a deck ({classId, cards, commander, companion}) to a short string and
back via battlecards/codec.js: a compact "cls~cmd~cmp~id*count|..." payload,
gzipped when CompressionStream is available (MPCKG1. prefix, ~halves it) else
raw base64url (MPCK1.). Card/class ids never contain the ~ * | . delimiters.
Both paths are node-safe so the round-trip is unit-tested.

Deck builder: "Copy Code" copies the current deck to the clipboard; "Import
Code" loads a pasted code (unknown class rejected, unknown cards skipped with a
count, then Review & Save).

Tests: tests/unit/codec_test.mjs (round-trip incl. gzip vs raw, dup counts,
loadout slots, garbage->null); tests/integration/deck_codes_smoke.mjs (headless
boot of deck.html proving the wiring loads and the export guard fires). Full
suite 196/196.

entries.title: Add Arena (draft) run mode
entries.body:
New feature: draft a 30-card deck one pick at a time, then run it against fresh AI
opponents until 3 losses (12 wins = a flawless run), for win-scaled rewards. Entry
via ?arena=1 and an Arena tile on the mode picker; the run persists + resumes like
the other run modes.

Built as a parallel mode alongside dungeon/heist/tombs/duels (the codebase's own
pattern), reusing the duels.js draft machinery and the shared overlay/UI:
- game.js: arenaRunMode flag + ARENA_KEY + load/save/clear; wired into the
  playerCount/heropower/mulligan guards, the gameOver hook, the concede handler, and
  the boot dispatch. New arena* functions mirror the duels* ones — but the deck is
  FIXED at the drafted 30 (no between-fight loot, unlike Duels), and it ends at 3
  losses only (12-win sweep caps it). genArenaEnemy builds a fair 30-card opponent
  via Duels.autoDraftDeck (no passives, matching the player). Reward: 100 + 120/win
  gold, 1600 for a 12-win sweep, plus the server pack.
- pickDuelsDraftOverlay gained a `size` param (default 10 keeps Duels byte-identical;
  Arena passes 30).
- start.html: an Arena mode tile (resume badge auto-detected).

Verified: headless arena_smoke.mjs drives hero -> power -> 30-card draft to a live
battle (7/7) — player on the drafted ~30 vs a full AI deck, run persisted, no
uncaught errors. Engine suite still 195/195.

entries.title: Strengthen the fuzz oracle: elimination/winner invariants + Felstring regression
entries.body:
Widen what validateGameState catches (it's the fuzzer's + nightly-fuzz's oracle),
being careful to add only HARD boundary invariants — a noisy oracle is worse than
a tight one.

Added to validateGameState (engine/validate.js), guarded like the existing
turn/priority checks:
- while the game is live, an eliminated seat keeps no board creatures and no weapon
  (checkGameOver clears them and summon/reborn skip the dead, so a lingering board
  or weapon on a dead seat is real corruption);
- a finished game names a valid, non-eliminated winner (or null for an FFA wipe).

Deliberately did NOT add two tempting-but-false ones the deep FFA fuzz flagged as
legal states: an eliminated seat's HAND can gain harmless dead cards from all-player
draws, and a live seat momentarily at <=0 life is a timing-dependent transient — both
are "soft" per the module's design, so neither is checked. (Also confirmed
mana.cur<=max is NOT an invariant — the Coin/Innervate push cur above max — and uid
uniqueness was already covered.)

Regression fixture: weapons_wave23_test now covers the exact nightly-fuzz-found crash
— Felstring Harp breaking on the same hit it heals (durability 1 -> 0, breakWeapon
nulls p.weapon, code then read healInsteadOnOwnTurn on null). Asserts no throw, still
heals +2, weapon breaks to null, state valid.

Verified: full suite 195/195; deep fuzz clean with the new invariants — 2p 201/0 and
FFA 251/0 (123k actions, zero false positives). The FFA self-elimination regression
was already locked in by ffa_duel_test.

entries.title: Add an adversarial fuzz of the host's guest-intent handler
entries.body:
The host applies UNTRUSTED guest intents via applyGuestIntent (turn-gated,
queue-guarded, seat-checked, try/catch-wrapped, and now server shape-validated) —
a path that was never fuzzed. game.js isn't node-importable (THREE/DOM), so this
boots ONE real host into a 3-human FFA and fuzzes applyGuestIntent in-browser.

Key setup insight: the two guests never connect, so their seats stay HUMAN (a
never-polled seat is never marked stale, so duel.aiSeats stays empty and intents
actually apply instead of being dropped as AI seats).

battlecards/tests/integration/relay_fuzz.mjs (standalone, needs Chrome) fires
1500 adversarial intents at window.__game.applyGuestIntent: junk/blank kinds,
invalid seats (host seat 0 / out-of-range / null / string), wrong-turn actions,
bad uids/targets. After EACH it asserts:
- it never throws (the try/catch holds),
- validateGameState(state) == 0 (no adversarial intent corrupts the game),
- the current player is never left eliminated unless the game is over,
- for an invalid seat, the state fingerprint is UNCHANGED — no cross-seat
  leakage or unauthorized mutation.

Exposes applyGuestIntent + duel on the window.__game test hook. validateGameState
is a test-only oracle (correctly NOT in the client E bundle), so the harness
dynamic-imports engine/validate.js into the page the same way the node suites
import it directly.

Result: 8/8, 0 findings (1500 intents — 32 applied, 511 invalid-seat rejections
checked, game stayed live) — the relay guard layer holds under a hostile intent
firehose. Reject-heavy by design: the engine fuzzer already covers legal moves;
this covers the untrusted-relay guards above them.

entries.title: Save resilience: extend the degrade-not-brick helper to the overworld
entries.body:
Follow-up to the battlecards save-resilience pass. New overworld/safestore.js (a
self-contained copy of battlecards/safestore.js — the two games ship from one
repo but keep separate import graphs) and routed the ENTIRE overworld JSON
persistence through it, so a corrupt blob falls back instead of throwing on load
and a quota-failed write returns false instead of throwing mid-save.

bag.js was the real gap: its money + bag WRITES (getMoney/earn/spend, getBag/
addItem/consume) had no try guard, so a full or blocked store threw straight out
of an inventory change. The rest (party, daycare, pokedex, settings, events,
items, trainers, main.js's box/pos/region/flypoints/playtime) were already
try-wrapped — resilient but silent — and are now uniform AND report a corrupt or
failed save through the window.reportErr beacon (→ errors.html).

Zero JSON.parse(localStorage) / localStorage.setItem remain in overworld/*.js.

Tests: safestore_test.mjs gains a drift guard that runs the same corrupt→fallback
+ quota→false assertions against BOTH copies (18). Full suite 192/192; every
edited overworld module node --check-clean. No overworld headless harness exists,
so validation was static (syntax + a semantic-equivalence review of each 1:1
JSON.parse→safeLoad / setItem→safeSave routing).

entries.title: Save resilience: localStorage that degrades instead of bricking
entries.body:
Two localStorage failure modes could kill a battlecards page outright:
- a CORRUPT/truncated blob -> JSON.parse throws on load -> the page that reads it
  (collection, deckbuilder, a saved run) dies before it renders;
- a FAILED write (quota exceeded, Safari private mode, storage disabled) ->
  setItem throws mid-flow -> the action that was saving (open a pack, save a deck,
  advance a run) blows up and can lose the very state it was storing.

Most reads were already try-wrapped, but EVERY write was unguarded against quota
and there was no observability when a save silently failed.

New battlecards/safestore.js:
- safeLoad(key, fallback): missing -> fallback (silent, normal); corrupt ->
  fallback + a reported anomaly.
- safeSave / safeSaveStr: never throw — a failed write returns false and is
  reported. Node-safe (no localStorage -> fallback / false).
Both surface through the window.reportErr beacon, so a real player's storage
trouble shows up on /errors.html instead of a dead page.

Routed the battlecards persistence through it: collection.js (the player's
collection / decks / gold — addToCollection was the one genuinely unguarded
corrupt-blob read), game.js run-state saves+loads (dungeon/heist/tombs/duels),
deck.js (slots + class), mpmode.js (auth token + cached state).

Tests: tests/unit/safestore_test.mjs (corrupt -> fallback + report, quota-write ->
false + report, no-storage path — 14, in run-all). The 3-browser relay harness
confirms game.js still boots + plays through the routed modules (23/23). Full
suite 192/192. Follow-up: the overworld's unguarded reads (bag/party/daycare) can
route through the same helper.

entries.title: Duel robustness: guest desync self-heal via a snapshot fingerprint
entries.body:
In the host-authoritative relay a guest applies its own move optimistically and
trusts the next host snapshot; fromSnapshot already IS the authoritative rebuild
each ingest, so play self-heals. But if a gameplay field ever silently dropped or
mangled on the wire (a nested card field, a non-JSON-safe type, a migration gap),
two clients would quietly diverge with NO signal.

Now the host stamps snap.digest = E.stateDigest(state) into every wire snapshot
(snapshotState / snapshotForDuel), and the guest recomputes it right after
fromSnapshot. A mismatch reports through the throttled window.reportErr beacon
(-> errors.html) and bumps duelDebug.desyncs. The rebuild already happened, so
the guest is on the best authoritative data — but the drift is now OBSERVABLE
instead of silent.

- engine/serialize.js: stateDigest(state) = FNV-1a over JSON.stringify(normalize(
  state)). normalize strips events/rng/cardsById and remaps uids, so the print is
  stream- and uid-agnostic: a faithful round-trip ALWAYS matches (zero false
  alarm) while any real divergence is caught. (Not computed inside toSnapshot --
  normalize calls toSnapshot, which would recurse.) fromSnapshot now drops the
  transport-only digest so it can't leak into a re-serialization.
- engine/core.js: re-export stateDigest through the engine.js aggregation.
- site/topbar.js: expose window.reportErr (reuses its dedup + hard cap).
- game.js: stamp the digest on publish; verify + report on ingest; duelDebug.desyncs;
  expose duelDebug on window.__game for the harness.

Effectively the snapshot-fidelity fuzz check, moved into the RUNTIME on real
production games.

Tests: serialize_test digest block -- clean round-trip matches, is stream-agnostic,
and dropped-card / off-by-one-life / wrong-active-seat each diverge (34). The
3-browser relay harness now asserts desyncs===0 across all live clients (20/20).
The harness ALSO caught what every node test missed: E.stateDigest was absent
from the browser bundle because core.js re-exports serialize via a NAMED list --
now fixed, with a node guard asserting the aggregated export exists. Full suite
190/190.

entries.title: FFA: hand the turn on when the active player eliminates itself
