- Slot logic (MY DECKS up to 40, new/edit/delete/name, save) carried over.

Fix: the Delete button had CSS display:none, so setting inline display='' fell
back to none and it never showed — now sets 'block'.

Verified headless: class prompt → pick class → real canvas tiles in both tabs,
mana filter + pager + search, tap-to-add with badge, save a full 40 into a slot,
delete button visible, mobile toggle opens the deck panel. 0 errors.

entries.title: Fix card-battle handshake: accept the CURRENT challenge type
entries.body:
Bug: if a challenge changed type before the target accepted (e.g. a Pokemon
challenge was replaced by a card one — the backend dedupes per sender), the
incoming dialog kept its stale label and ran the stale accept branch. Pressing
Accept then ran the Pokemon path while the backend only had a card challenge,
so the challenger got pulled into a card duel while the accepter tried to load
a nonexistent Pokemon match — "card battle never launched."

Fix:
- acceptChallengeFrom() re-reads the stored challenge type at accept time and
  routes trade/card/pokemon off that, so a stale dialog can't accept the wrong
  battle. The Pokemon path also falls back to goCardDuel if the backend returns
  a cardmatch.
- pollChallenges() now refreshes an on-screen challenge dialog when the pending
  challenge's type or sender changes, so the label matches what will actually
  launch.

Verified: overworld boots clean. Live two-client card handshake still needs a
realm re-test.

entries.title: Decks: 40 deck slots, Mage Starter seed, delete + empty-state
entries.body:
Deck storage moves from one-per-class to a list of up to 40 named PvP deck
slots (user.decks: [{id,name,classId,cards}]).

Backend (mp.mjs):
- normalizeDecks() migrates the old per-class object to slots one-time; legacy
  10-card starter decks are dropped, and if that leaves none you get a 40-card
  Mage Starter. New accounts start with the Mage Starter too. So both test
  accounts get a ready mage deck and can skip building.
- save-deck creates/updates a slot by id (cap 40, "slots full" past that);
  delete-deck removes one. reset-deck removed. Mage Starter validated against
  the real pool (exactly 40, mage/neutral, within copy caps).

Client:
- Deck builder is now slot-based: MY DECKS list (up to 40), ＋ New Deck, per-deck
  name, Save (create/update), Delete This Deck. Class stays the first choice.
  Free-play stores slots in localStorage (migrating the old single deck).
- Overworld card battle reads the slot array; with no valid 40-card deck it
  shows "You have no decks :(" and blocks the battle (both challenger and
  accepter). Deck-select labels show the deck name.

Verified: slot lifecycle headless (build→save→new→edit→delete, 0 errors);
backend slot/migration/cap/delete logic unit-tested against pool-rarity.json;
overworld boots clean.

entries.title: Decks: 40-card class-based PvP constructed + class-first builder
entries.body:
Constructed/PvP decks are now 40 cards (was 30 free-play / 10 MP). Players
build their own from their collection; DECK_SIZE=40 in collection.js and the
MP backend (mp.mjs) validates 40. Overworld card-battle deck selection
(openDeckSelect + cardParty) now requires a full 40-card deck.

Dungeon runs are fully separated: dungeonStarterDeck() always uses the stock
10-card Dungeon.STARTER_DECKS and never reads the account's PvP decks, so a
dungeon deck can't leak into PvP and vice-versa.

Deckbuilder polish — class is the FIRST choice:
- No "all cards" option; you pick a class before anything shows.
- With no class the collection is a prompt ("choose your class"); picking one
  filters to neutral + that class (+ duals) and loads any deck saved for it.
- Switching class prunes off-class cards from the working deck.
- Count reads "/ 40"; save/auto-fill require a class; MP save stores a 40-card
  PvP deck per class ("take it into card battles").

Verified headless: builder boots to a class prompt at 0/40, picking Mage
filters the grid, no errors; overworld still boots clean.

entries.title: Rules: MTG hand-size cleanup + tokens exile on death
entries.body:
Hand size (MAX_HAND 15): drawing/gaining a card past 15 no longer burns it.
The hand may exceed 15 during your turn; at end of turn you discard down to 15,
MTG-style — YOUR choice which cards (human via the discard modal, AI dumps its
priciest). Replaces the old auto-pop-newest trim. Removed the burn-on-overdraw
in drawCards/addCardToHand/addCoin and the silent < MAX_HAND drops on
return-to-hand / copy-spell / conjure effects.

Tokens: instantiate() now carries the token flag, and every summoned token
(inline opt-summons included) is marked token:true. toGraveyard exiles any
token — summoned creatures, Blood/Clue/Food/Treasure — instead of sending it to
the graveyard, so tokens leave no corpse and can't be reanimated, referenced,
or reshuffled. Coins are NOT tokens and still go to the graveyard (reshuffle).

Verified in-engine: overdraw to 29 with no burn; end-of-turn queues a 14-card
choose-your-discard down to 15; deck-out reshuffles the graveyard (tokens
excluded); a summoned token dies to exile, not the graveyard.

entries.title: MP: RuneScape-style player trade (phase 4)
entries.body:
Backend (mp.mjs): trade requests reuse the challenge inbox (type 'trade');
trade-accept opens a trade:<id> blob { a,b,offerA,offerB,acceptA,acceptB,
done,cancelled }; trade-mine (requester discovery), trade-poll, trade-offer
(any change unlocks both sides), trade-lock (both accepted -> execute + done),
trade-cancel. Cards + packs are validated and swapped server-side; Pokemon and
bag items are echoed in the blob so each client applies its own local swap.

Client (overworld/main.js): startTrade sends a request and waits for the peer
to open; incoming 'trade' request accepts via trade-accept. Full trade window
with YOUR/THEIR offer panels, category tabs (Cards/Packs/Pokemon/Items),
add/remove from your inventory, ACCEPT lock (resets on any change), 800ms
poll, and applyTradeSwap (removes given party/box mons + bag items, adds
received; refreshes the card collection/packs).

Verified: overworld boots clean, 0 errors. Live two-client + deployed backend
still needs an in-realm test.

entries.title: Overworld MP: deck-selection phase before a card duel (phase 3)
entries.body:
Before a card battle starts, each player picks which class deck to bring.
openDeckSelect lists the account's decks (10+ cards) and calls back with the
chosen one; both the challenger (sendCardChallenge) and the accepter route
through it. Auto-picks silently when only one deck qualifies.

entries.title: Overworld MP: walk up to a player to challenge or trade (phases 1-2)
entries.body:
Press Z facing another player's on-map sprite (ghost) to open a menu:
Pokemon Battle / Card Battle / Trade / Cancel. Battle options route into the
existing challenge->accept handshakes (sendChallenge / sendCardChallenge); the
incoming side (showIncoming) already handles both. Trade is a stub for phase 4.

- ghostAt(tx,ty) finds a friend-ghost on a tile; interact() opens playerMenu
  when you face one (MP only).
- playerMenu wired into key dispatch, draw, tap, and menu-blocking.

entries.title: Gibberling snowballs properly
entries.body:
Add summonId support to the summon effect: instantiate a real card def so the
summoned token keeps its own ongoing. Gibberling's Spellburst now summons a
real Gibberling (with Spellburst), so each spell grows the board (1->2->3->4,
verified) instead of making an inert 1/1.

entries.title: import 12 Scholomance Academy cards (+ Cub token)
entries.body:
New cards (none already in pool), with wiki art:
- Ras Frostwhisper, Cram Session, Brain Freeze (Combo), Molten Blast,
  Boneweb Egg, Survival of the Fittest (buff-zones), Onyx Magescribe
  (Spellburst), Adorable Infestation, Manafeeder Panthara, Groundskeeper,
  Diligent Notetaker (Spellburst), Gibberling.

Small engine additions: conditional predicates heroPowerUsed +
holdingSpellMinCost; a return-played-spell effect in runSecretEffects (for
Spellburst "return the spell"). Spellburst reuses the once-per spell-played
ongoing; buff-zones/combo already existed.

Verified live: end-of-turn AoE, Combo (freeze+3), buff-zones (board & hand
+4/+4), heroPowerUsed & holdingSpellMinCost conditionals both directions,
Spellburst conjure, and Notetaker returning the real cast spell. Gibberling
summons a plain 1/1 (inline summon can't carry its own Spellburst, so it
doesn't infinitely snowball).

entries.title: EVH import batch 2 — 5 cards, faithfully wired
entries.body:
Add (with wiki art + 3 small engine additions):
- Ball and Chain (1 warrior weapon): Deathrattle buff your DAMAGED minions
  +1/+2 (new buff requireDamaged filter).
- Widow's Bite (2 druid): hero +1 Atk this turn, +1 Armor, add Widow's Feast
  -> Widow's Banquet chain (two new token spells).
- Bone Flurry (2 DK): 3 dmg split among enemies; if a friendly minion died
  this turn, 3 more (new conditional friendlyDied).
- Crowd Control (3 warrior): 2 dmg to all minions; +2 more if deck >= 25 (new
  conditional deckAtLeast).
- Getaway Hogdriver (5 neutral Quilboar): Battlecry draw 2; if both minions,
  gain Charge (new draw-check effect).

Verified live: buff hits only damaged, deck>=25 doubles, both-minions grants
Charge, Widow's Feast is added. Skipped Disguised Watchman (Disguise) and
Molten Gold (cast-3-spells transform) — both need bespoke mechanics.

entries.title: EVH import batch 1 — IMPFERNAL! + fix two stubs
entries.body:
- Add IMPFERNAL! (6-mana 6/6 neutral epic Demon; Deathrattle: 3 damage to all
  other characters) with wiki art.
- Fix Specter of Despair: its Taunt/"Can't attack" were text-only (it could
  actually attack) -> keywords taunt + pacifist.
- Fix Arachnathid: Rush + "friendly minions Poisonous" were text-only ->
  keyword rush + poisonous aura.
Lotus Bookie and Sewer Imp were already wired correctly.

entries.title: add Concealing Confection (neutral common Mech)
entries.body:
1-mana 1/2 Mech: Deathrattle - get a random weapon (conjure-random weapon).
Art from the supplied Concealing_Confection_full.jpg.

entries.title: consolidate to one Colaque's Shell
entries.body:
Remove the stray collectible duplicate (colaque_s_shell) — nothing summoned
or referenced it. Keep token_colaques_shell, the actual appendage Colaque
summons. Also drop its art + pool-rarity entry.

entries.title: rename "Mechanical" tribe -> "Mech"
entries.body: 22 cards folded into the existing Mech tribe.

entries.title: move Colaque's Shell into Appendages
entries.body:
Tag the collectible colaque_s_shell creature with colossalOf: Colaque so it
buckets under Appendages alongside the generated token.

entries.title: Overworld: don't take a stray step out of a battle
entries.body:
A movement key held when an encounter started (or a keyup missed during the
battle) stayed in heldKeys, so the frame combat ended the loop read it and
stepped once. Flush heldKeys on the battle/PvP -> not-blocking transition, so
the player stops after combat (a still-held key re-registers via key-repeat).

entries.title: Mica, Wanderknight - line break before Spell Damage
Idol of Y'Shaarj is a 10/10 creature (Battlecry summons a 10/10)
entries.body:
Was an 8-mana sorcery; now a 10/10 Priest creature whose Battlecry summons a
10/10 Idol of Y'Shaarj token. The token (token_idol_of_y_shaarj) gets a copy
of the idol's art so it looks identical; it has no battlecry, so no loop.

entries.title: drop the "Static:" prefix on planes
entries.body: The persistent effect line stands on its own between Arrival and Chaos.

entries.title: add 8 Planechase-style planes + 3 plane static mechanisms
entries.body:
New planes (Arrival/Static/Chaos/Departure), adapted from MTG planes into the
game's idiom:
- Krosa (all creatures +2/+2), Sokenzan (all +1/+1 & Rush), The Hippodrome
  (all -5 Attack) -> new plane "aura" staticRule wired into recomputeAuras.
- Stronghold Furnace (combat damage doubled) -> new "double-damage" rule in
  resolveCombat.
- Lethe Lake (turn-start mill), Takenuma (creature dies -> owner draws),
  Fields of Summer (cast -> gain life), Minamo (cast -> draw) -> general
  plane "trigger" staticRule fired at turn-start / sweepDeaths / spell-cast.
drawCards already handled; effects reuse existing types (draw/mill/heal/
damage/summon/destroy-random/bounce).

keywords.js: scope the plane vocabulary (Arrival/Chaos/Departure/Static) so a
plane's "Static:" shows the plane meaning while the combat Static keyword
still reads as paralyze on creatures.

Verified live: auras (5/5, 0/3, 4/4+Rush), doubled combat (6), death-draw,
cast-draw, cast-life, turn-start mill — all correct, 0 errors. Planes bucket
now lists 14.

entries.title: Backstab is a Rogue card (was bounty_hunter)
Ancient Watcher - Defender & Pacifist on line 1, Inspire below
Ancient Watcher uses the Pacifist keyword
entries.body:
Its "Can't Attack" was text-only (never enforced). Add the pacifist keyword
(engine already blocks attacks for it) and reword the card to "Pacifist."

entries.title: rename Savannah Lions -> Godsbreath Tyrant + Beast tribe
entries.body: Kept the id (savannah_lions) so any art reference stays intact.

entries.title: Coin & Banana are non-collectible but not tokens (reshuffle)
entries.body:
They were flagged token:true, which both hid them AND made them cease to
exist on deck reshuffle. Split those concerns:
- Coin & Banana: drop token, add collectible:false.
- All pool/collection/discover/generation filters now also exclude
  collectible:false (so they stay out of decks, the collectible pool, random
  generation, and are hidden in the gallery — unchanged behavior).
- The graveyard-reshuffle filter keys on token only, so Coin & Banana now
  reshuffle back into the deck; true tokens (Blood/Clue/Food/Treasure) still
  cease to exist. viewer isUncollectible + cardart honor collectible:false.

Verified: Coin/Banana reshuffle; Blood Token does not; they stay in Generic
and never appear under a collectible class.

entries.title: Treasure Token -> Token tribe; Coin & Banana -> Generic
entries.body:
- Treasure Token gets tribe "Token" (so it joins Generic and exiles instead
  of graveyarding, like Blood/Clue/Food).
- The Coin and Banana bucket into uncollectible Generic by id (kept as plain
  neutral token spells — no tribe/exile change). Generic is now 21.

entries.title: Token tribe -> Generic + exile-instead-of-graveyard
entries.body:
- Tag Blood Token, Clue Token, Food Token with tribe "Token".
- systemBucket buckets any Token-tribe card into uncollectible Generic
  (gallery + viewer), so those three move out of their class into Generic.
- toGraveyard now exiles Token-tribe cards instead of adding them to the
  graveyard (no corpse, unreanimatable). Verified in a live game: a Token
  creature dying lands in exile; a normal creature still goes to graveyard.

entries.title: optional draws — `may` prompt + draw-success gating
entries.body:
Add a reusable optional-decision mechanism so "you may …" effects actually
prompt and can be declined, and gate follow-ups on a real draw:
- drawCards() now returns the number of cards that reached hand.
- new effect `draw-then`: draw N, run `then` only if a card was drawn.
- new effect `may` + state.askQueue + resolveAsk(): defers a yes/no to the
  controller; AI auto-takes it (resolveAIAsks), the human gets a centered
  Draw/Pass popup (openAskModal, reusing the choose-one decision menu), with
  multiplayer guest relay (k:'ask').
- Arcane Artisan now uses may -> draw-then -> damage, so you may draw, and
  each opponent loses 1 Life only if you actually drew.

Verified in a live game: casting an Arcane spell (with an artifact) prompts;
Draw -> deck -1 and opponent -1; Pass -> no change; nothing happens until the
choice is made.

entries.title: add Arcane Artisan (sorcerer rare) + conditional trigger support
entries.body:
3-mana 3/3 Human Wizard: if you control an artifact or enchantment, whenever
you cast an Arcane spell, draw a card and each opponent loses 1 Life.

Wired as a spell-played ongoing gated by two new ongoingCondOk checks:
- cond.school: the played spell's school (schoolOf) must match (Arcane)
- cond.controlArtEnch: caster must control an artifact or enchantment
Both are additive and unused elsewhere, so no regression. Verified in a live
game: fires only with an artifact + Arcane spell (draw + opponent -1 Life),
gated off otherwise. Art cropped from the supplied card image.

entries.title: add Furious Lutrin (barbarian common)
entries.body:
3-mana 2/2 Beast. Alliance (creature-played -> buff-self +1/+1) via ongoings,
Frenzy (self-damaged, once/survives -> draw 2) via ongoing so the damage
handler fires it exactly once. Art cropped from the supplied card image.

entries.title: reorder Triumphant Troubadour tribes to Angel Barbarian Bard
put Swing / Frenzy abilities on their own lines
entries.body:
- Gogogo Goram: Swing ability on its own line below Trample & Magnetic.
- Triumphant Troubadour: Frenzy on its own line, separate from Lifesteal.

entries.title: add Odd Minstrel (neutral epic collectible)
entries.body:
3-mana 2/4 neutral Human Bard: Divine Shield & Elusive; Deathrattle adds a
coin to each player's hand (gain-coin + give-enemy-card). Art cropped from
the supplied card image into art/odd_minstrel.jpg + indexed.

entries.title: excavate spells have no spell school
entries.body:
Remove the "Fel" spell school (tribe) from Azerite Fragment, Fool's Azerite,
Azerite Chunk, and Azerite Gem. They stay plain sorceries with no school.

entries.title: flag the 4 excavate dig spells into Excavate
entries.body:
Mark Azerite Fragment, Fool's Azerite, Azerite Chunk, and Azerite Gem with
excavate:true so they join the Excavate section (25 total). They keep their
rarities (uncommon/common/rare/epic) via the existing showsRarity rule.

entries.title: Battlecards/wiki: new Excavate uncollectible section (keeps rarity)
entries.body:
- Mark the 21 Azerite class legendaries with excavate:true.
- Add an "Excavate" bucket to the gallery/viewer uncollectible group, keyed
  off the excavate flag (checked first in systemBucket so these come out of
  their class sections).
- Unlike other uncollectible cards, excavate cards keep their rarity: add
  showsRarity(card) (collectible OR excavate) and use it for the rarity gem
  on the face and the "· Rarity" text in the wiki meta + viewer type-line.

entries.title: reword Champion of the Parish
entries.body: "gain a +1/+1 counter" -> "this gains +1/+1".

entries.title: delete Zilliax Deluxe 3000
entries.body:
Remove the card from cards.json and its orphaned art-manifest entry. No
code, deck, pack, or module references pointed at it. The base Zilliax
card is unaffected.

entries.title: delete Boomtown Claim, Crossroads Station, Gold Vein, Hallowed Springs
entries.body:
Remove the four bounty_hunter lands from cards.json. No code, deck, pack,
or conjure references pointed at them.

entries.title: fix Alara text — split the coin-parity static effect out of Arrival
entries.body:
The persistent coin-flip clause was bundled into the Arrival line. Move it
to its own line and reword: at the start of each player's turn they flip a
coin — heads blocks odd-cost cards, tails blocks even-cost cards this turn.
Display-only; the coin-parity staticRule already drives the mechanic. Not
prefixed "Static:" since Static is a separate combat keyword.

entries.title: Battlecards/wiki: catalog dungeon-run emblems under Generic
entries.body:
- Add the 14 dungeon-run treasures (Potion of Vitality, Crystal Gem,
  Captured Flag, Battle Totem, etc.) to cards.json as neutral,
  non-collectible 'emblem' cards mirroring dungeon.js TREASURES.
- Bucket type === 'emblem' into the Generic uncollectible section in the
  gallery and in-game viewer, alongside Blood Gem.

entries.title: Battlecards/wiki: Planes uncollectible category + one ability per line
entries.body:
- Add "Planes" bucket to the gallery/viewer Uncollectible group (type
  === 'plane'); planes now hidden from the collectible pool by default.
- Reformat all 6 plane descriptions so each ability (Arrival / Chaos /
  Departure) starts on its own line, matching the land formatting.

entries.title: Battlecards/wiki: Advanced Lands section + Chrome Cat as neutral collectible
entries.body:
- Add "Advanced Lands" gallery/viewer bucket for the 8 Abzan cards
  conjured by the Abzan land theme (magepunk-class cards whose name
  matches a conjure-named land theme).
- Generic bucket now contains only Blood Gem.
- Chrome Cat: neutral common collectible creature (removed C color /
  wubrg set), tribe changed Cat -> "Mech Beast" (renders as Mech + Beast).

entries.title: Cards: fold deathknight into death_knight (alias + retag 8 cards)
entries.body:
Same fix as the demon_hunter variants: add a canonClass alias so the
mislabeled "deathknight" folds onto death_knight for naming/colour/grouping,
and correct the 8 source tags to "death_knight". Death Knight is now 77
cards with one gallery option; game boots, 0 errors.

entries.title: Keywords: bold Bushido (gains +1/+1 when it attacks)
entries.body: Cascade and Miniaturize stay unbolded — confirmed unimplemented.

entries.title: Keywords: bold Medic & Luck, plus 21 other mechanics that were plain text
entries.body:
Add glossary entries (bold + hover explanation) for keywords that were
showing up as ordinary text on card faces. Requested: Medic, Luck. From a
scan of every card's rules text for keyword-like terms not already bolded,
also added the ones confirmed as real mechanics in the engine: Ward, Scry,
Gaze, Prowess, Avenge, Frenzy, Overheal, Outcast, Corrupt, Colossal, Echo,
Spellburst, Constellation, Alliance, Quickdraw, Mill, Arrival, Departure,
Chaos, Regenerate, Ephemeral. Tooltips match the engine behaviour (e.g.
Medic = heal neighbours at end of turn, Luck = coin flip). Verified they
bold with no false positives (Fire/Beast/"toward" stay plain).

entries.title: Lands: one ability per line + show the Sacrifice: Draw a card ability
entries.body:
Land card text ran every ability together and never showed the universal
"Sacrifice this land: Draw a card." ability (which the engine already
supports — sacrificeLand draws 1). Reformat all 81 land descriptions so
each ⟳ ability sits on its own line (richTokens already turns \n into a
line break) and append the sacrifice line. Also give the wiki's card
detail panel white-space: pre-line so those breaks show there too. No
engine change — the sacrifice ability was always functional, just unlisted.

entries.title: data: retag the 19 mislabeled Demon Hunter cards to demon_hunter
entries.body:
Corrected the source cardClass values (17 "demonhunter", 1
"demonhunter_free", 1 "demon_hunter_free") to "demon_hunter" so the cards
are Demon Hunter at the data level, not just folded for display. Demon
Hunter is now 75 cards; no stray free/demonhunter tags remain. JSON
re-validated, game boots, galleries show one Demon Hunter section.

entries.title: inspect cards in play too, not just cards in hand
entries.body:
Clicking a card on the field now shows it big in the left inspect panel,
same as clicking a hand card — your own creatures/locations, the
opponent's creatures/walkers, and works on the opponent's turn as well.
For your own creatures the click still arms an attack; the inspect just
rides alongside as a read-only view. A face-down (disguised) enemy is not
revealed. The inspect auto-close now keys off the card leaving play
entirely rather than leaving your hand, so a field card's inspect stays up
until it dies or you click away. Live stats/modifiers show (e.g. a buffed
3/4 with "Modifiers +2/+3").

entries.title: make choose-one/adventure/trade a centered, backdrop popup
entries.body:
The choose-one engine works, but the decision menu popped up small at the
drop point — often near the cluttered hero-panel/hand area — while the
dropped card snapped back to hand. Any stray board click ran
hideWalkerMenu and dismissed it, so the card just sat in hand with no
choice ever made ("goes right back to my hand, never get the choice").

Route hand-play decisions (choose one, adventure, trade) through a
centered popup over a dimmed backdrop: large buttons, always in the same
obvious spot regardless of where the card is dropped, and the backdrop
absorbs off-menu clicks (cancels the decision) so a board click can't
silently dismiss it. Verified with real deck-drawn instances: Druid of the
Claw / Keeper of the Grove / Power of the Wild all open the centered menu
and resolve (Keeper's damage choice arms targeting as expected); backdrop
click cancels; drop location no longer matters.

entries.title: fix drops onto the hero-panel area being cancelled
entries.body:
Root cause of "can't play Druid of the Claw — it goes back to my hand and
I never get the choose-one": the drag-to-play zone used a fixed height
cutoff (innerHeight*0.80). The 3D hero panel now sits at ~0.78-0.89 of the
height, so releasing a dragged card onto the panel area landed in the
"cancel" band — the card returned to hand and, for a choose-one, the
choice menu never opened. Affected every card, but showed up most on
5-drops like Druid of the Claw that get dropped lower.

A drag now plays wherever it lands EXCEPT when released back onto one of
your own hand cards (detected by raycast), with a generous bottom-edge
cap. The drag hint/place-marker follow the same rule. Verified: dropping
Druid of the Claw on the panel area opens the choice menu and plays it;
dropping back on the hand still cancels; normal drag-play unaffected.

entries.title: add Play actions to the inspect panel (fixes choose-one cards)
entries.body:
Choose-one cards (Druid of the Claw etc.) could only be resolved by
dragging them out — the choice menu never appears on a click, and the
inspect view had no way to act, so clicking one was a dead end. The
choose-one engine works fine (verified via drag); this was a
discoverability gap.

The inspect panel now shows action buttons for a playable hand card:
one button per branch for a Choose One, Summon/Cast for an Adventure,
Play (+ Trade) otherwise. Buttons re-enable pointer events on the
otherwise click-through panel and route through the same play logic
(targeting/pending included). Dragging still works for everything.
Verified: click->inspect->choice plays Druid of the Claw with the right
effect; the plain Play button plays a normal creature; 0 errors.

entries.title: drop the hero panel slightly so it fully clears the land slots
entries.body:
The panel's top edge still just grazed the bottom of the land row. Lower
its world Y (1.12 -> 0.92) so it hangs a touch further down, leaving a
clean gap above it. Only the human panel moves; the hand cards still
depth-sort in front of it.

entries.title: raise the land row so it clears the 3D hero panel
entries.body:
The land slots (z 4.0) sat right where the hero panel (z 5.15) projects,
so the panel rode over the slot row. Move LAND_Z up to 3.05 (farther from
the camera, between the artifact row and the hero) so the slots project
clearly above the panel with a real gap. Land-shop click detection follows
the same slot markers, so nothing functional changes.

entries.title: render your hero panel as a 3D object so the hand sorts in front
entries.body:
The hero panel was a DOM node, which a WebGL hand can never truly render
in front of. Render it in-scene instead: a camera-billboarded plane with a
canvas texture (life, class, mana, deck, gear, portrait, class-power orb),
positioned between your land row and hand at a depth the hand cards sit in
front of — real per-pixel layering, no transparency tricks. The panel now
stays fully visible during your turn with cards correctly overlapping it.

Interactions preserved via raycast: the orb (kept in the panel's top band,
above the card overlap) fires the class power; the body arms a hero attack
or picks yourself as a spell/attack target; heroPanelAt hit-tests the mesh
so self-targeted spells work. Border colour reflects turn/armed/targetable
state and the texture repaints on state changes and async portrait loads.
The DOM panel is hidden in play (body.threed-hero) and kept only for the
read-only spectator view. Verified: orb→power, panel→self-target, a full
game, and inspect/drag all clean with 0 errors.

entries.title: hide hero panel behind the hand (no transparency); clear the lands
entries.body:
Per feedback: while the hand is up the panel should sit behind the cards,
not show through them as a translucent overlay, and it must not overlap
the land slots. A DOM panel can't render behind WebGL cards (the opaque
board would hide it), so instead the panel now hides entirely while the
hand is up — cards fully in front, no ghosting — and returns solid only
when the hand is minimized. Dropped its top below the projected land row
so it never overlaps the slots. It also stays visible during spell/attack
targeting (so your own hero is clickable) and on the opponent's turn.

entries.title: hand covers the hero panel; field-click tucks it away
entries.body:
The hand renders in the WebGL canvas and the panel is a DOM node, so the
canvas hand literally cannot paint over the panel. Approximate the wanted
look with a handMini state: while the hand is up it overlaps the panel
and the panel dims to 0.32 (hand reads in front); pressing anywhere on the
field tucks the hand down into a peeking row and the panel goes solid and
fully readable below the land slots. Reaching toward the hand (cursor in
the bottom strip) or pressing a hand card pops it back up, and a new turn
auto-raises it. Also compacted the panel so a minimized hand has room
below it. Verified: drag-to-play and click-inspect still work; approaching
the hand re-expands it so cards behind the solid panel stay reachable.

entries.title: center your hero panel between your lands and hand
entries.body:
Your hero/hero-power panel was CSS-pinned to the bottom-left corner while
every opponent's panel tracks their projected hero position (centered on
their slice, between their land row and hand). Position #my-panel the
same way — project heroPos(HUMAN) each frame and center the panel on it
(translate -50%,-50%) — so your hero mirrors the opponents'. Hero-attack
targeting and the power orb still work on the moved panel.

entries.title: clear the chat log when a new game starts
entries.body:
The in-battle chat overlay stays mounted across games (per-user room),
so messages from the previous game lingered into the next one. Add
Chat.clear() — wipes the visible rows (and their fade timers) without
resetting seen/lastTs, so old messages don't re-fetch on the next poll —
and call it from start() alongside the other new-game resets.

entries.title: dragged card no longer blocks drop-on-target raycast
entries.body:
Found while play-testing: dropping a targeted spell directly onto an
enemy creature never cast on it — it always fell back to arming the aim
arrow (requiring a second click). The dragged card floats under the
cursor, and pick() raycast against ALL entities, so it hit the dragged
card itself instead of the creature behind it; resolveDropTarget got the
card (not in the target list) and returned null. pick() now takes an
excludeUid and skips the card being dragged, threaded through the drag
hover, resolveDropTarget, and the magnetic-merge check. Verified: 6/6
targeted drags across 6 games now cast on drop; also fixes magnetic
Mech-merge by drag.

entries.title: repaint inspect panel when card art / mana font loads
entries.body:
Same class of bug as the 0-health fix: drawCardFace draws a procedural
fallback (placeholder art, fallback cost pip) until the card's art image
and the Mana font finish loading. The 3D cards repaint via artListeners
(refreshFace); the static inspect canvas was drawn once and never
updated, so it could show fallback art indefinitely. Subscribe to
artListeners while the panel is open and repaint the face in place; the
listener is removed on close (verified no leak). Also factored the stat
opts into inspectFaceOpts() shared by the initial draw and the repaint.

entries.title: fix inspect panel showing 0 health for hand creatures
entries.body:
drawCardFace reads health from opts.hp ?? card.health, but a creature in
hand carries its health in maxHealth (card.health is undefined), so the
inspect panel rendered 0. Pass the same stat opts the 3D card faces use
(hp: E.hp(card), maxHealth, and health: card.maxHealth on the copy).

entries.title: drag-to-play + click-to-inspect (Hearthstone-style)
entries.body:
Clicking a hand card no longer plays it — the old code cast spells on
press and played creatures on a tap, causing accidental plays. Now a
click/tap opens a pinned full-size inspect panel (art + rules + keyword
breakdown), and playing requires dragging the card up out of the hand
onto the field. The card follows the cursor while dragging, with a live
release hint; creatures drop into a board gap, targeted spells cast on
whatever they're dropped on (or arm the aiming arrow), and adventure/
choice/tradeable cards open their menus at the drop point. Inspect also
works on the opponent's turn.

entries.title: overworld: Pokemon followers (lead mon walks behind you)
entries.body:
Uses the Following-Pokemon walk sheets (data/pokemon_follow/<id>.png, 4x4
grid built by import_follower_walk.py) for the 896 species that have art. The
lead party member trails one tile behind on the player's path (HG/SS style),
faces its movement direction, animates its walk, keeps pace when you run/bike,
and hides while surfing. New FOLLOWERS option (on by default) toggles it live;
refreshFollower re-seeds it on map load / party change.

Verified: Treecko trails the player correctly; content/menus/options/hoenn/
story suites green (fixed a timing-only flake in the evolution content test).

entries.title: overworld: use PokemonZero Following-Pokemon pack (896 mon overworld sprites)
entries.body:
The Radical Ransei Characters folder only had 49 overworld charsets; the real
add-on is PokemonZero2024's Following-Pokemon pack (1126 charsets named by
species). Reconverted keyed by our species id -> data/pokemon_ow/<id>.png
(896 that match our dex, incl. all standard legendaries/mons; Ransei fakemon
aren't in the pack). drawLegendary now looks sprites up by species id, not dex.

entries.title: overworld: visible legendary sprites (Radical Ransei overworld art)
entries.body:
Converted the 49 Ransei Essentials overworld charsets to standalone Pokemon
overworld sprites (front-facing pose, trimmed, 40px tall) in data/pokemon_ow/
<dex>.png. The static legendaries now DRAW their sprite at their tile
(drawLegendary, keyed by dex on LEGENDARY_ENCOUNTERS) instead of being an
invisible trigger — you see Rayquaza/Kyogre/Groudon and walk up to battle.

Verified via screenshots (Kyogre in the Marine Cave pool, Rayquaza atop Sky
Pillar); 0 errors.

entries.title: overworld: give dive-able deep water a distinct look
entries.body:
The Emerald->web tileset flattens all sea to one ocean behavior, so dive
routes looked identical to ordinary water. Render a subtle darker, gently
shimmering tint over the surfable water of any map that offers a dive overlay
(isDiveMap), so the sea you can DIVE into reads as deeper/distinct. Purely
visual (drawn over the baked bottom layer); no data or collision change.

entries.title: overworld: faithful HM field moves via the party menu
entries.body:
HMs (incl. Dive) are now triggered the way the games do: you must have a
POKeMON that KNOWS the move, pick it from the PARTY menu's action list, and
it only does something in a valid spot. Selecting a party member opens an
action menu listing the field moves it knows (CUT/FLY/SURF/STRENGTH/FLASH/
ROCK SMASH/WATERFALL/DIVE) plus SUMMARY/SWITCH; each handler validates the
tile/facing (surf at water's edge, cut a tree, smash a rock, strength near a
boulder, dive on a dive route, waterfall on a fall, flash in a dark map, fly
outdoors) or explains why it can't.

- The 8 HMs are granted in the bag on a new game and are reusable (kind 'hm',
  never consumed); teach them to compatible mons via the bag.
- STRENGTH must be used before boulders will budge (reset per map).
- Bare interact no longer auto-uses HMs — it points you at the right move.
- Removed the ad-hoc 'v' dive key (bike stays on 'c').

Verified via _hm.js (grant/detect/validity/dive) + updated content/strength/
menus/menus2 suites; hoenn/story/battle green.

entries.title: overworld: add Mach Bike (Sky Pillar) + Dive traversal
entries.body:
Bike: a free field toggle (C key) — faster movement, and the only way across
Sky Pillar's cracked floors. The web engine doesn't model floor-collapse so
those tiles read as normal floor; gate them explicitly on player.biking
(behavior 0xD2, which only occurs in Sky Pillar, so no collateral). Surfing
dismounts the bike; a hud hint points players to the bike when a cracked
floor stops them. With the bike the full 1F->Top climb is traversable, so
Rayquaza is reachable.

Dive: dive/emerge are overlay map connections (offset 0) the engine
previously discarded. V key plunges from the surface to the underwater twin
at the same tile (needs a Water-type, like Surf) and surfaces back. Gated on
the map offering a dive/emerge connection rather than a deep-water behavior,
since the Emerald->web tileset flattens all sea to one ocean behavior.

Verified: walk blocked at cracked floor / bike crosses; full Sky Pillar climb
connects; Route 105 dive->Underwater_Route105->emerge round-trips; content/
strength/fly/hoenn/story suites all green.

entries.title: overworld: make Kyogre and Groudon reachable
entries.body:
Both caves were islands: Emerald places their entrances via the
abnormal-weather roaming system (unimplemented), and the entrances' exits
point at the dead MAP_DYNAMIC warp.

Terra Cave (Groudon): entry from Route 114 already fires (warp tiles are
always passable), so just repoint the entrance's MAP_DYNAMIC exit back to
Route 114. Move the Groudon encounter from the solid statue tile (17,22) to
its standable approach tile (17,26).

Marine Cave (Kyogre): fully isolated (no static route link, Dive unimpl),
so add a two-way warp between a reachable Route 105 island tile (11,21) and
Marine Cave End, landing on floor (9,26) with a surf path up to Kyogre.

Verified: both caves reachable from Littleroot (BFS), full enter->reach->
exit loops resolve, legendary tiles reachable by walk+surf flood, triggers
fire with right species; Hoenn suite 12/12.

entries.title: overworld: make Hoenn box legendaries catchable
entries.body:
The decomp catches Rayquaza/Kyogre/Groudon through an awakening cutscene +
a legendary-battle special the web engine doesn't run, and their overworld
sprites aren't in the build, so a region-picker could never actually catch
them. Add LEGENDARY_ENCOUNTERS: a real catchable wild battle placed on each
legendary's tile (walk onto it or face-and-interact) at L70, gated by a
caught/defeated flag so it doesn't repeat. Decoupled from the plot awakening
scenes (which stay seeded off — they assume story state and lead to no
catch). Verified: all three fire with the right species, gate after caught,
0 errors; Hoenn/Johto/story suites still green.

entries.title: overworld: seed Hoenn forced-story scene vars for the region-picker
entries.body:
Emerald coord_events were already extracted (unlike Crystal), but only two
Littleroot intro vars were seeded. Many other maps gate forced story
cutscenes on a per-map/route state var that vanilla starts at 0, so a
region-picker (who never runs the linear plot) would cold-fire them:
Oldale's researcher shoving you back off the sandy path, Petalburg's gym
tour + Scott, Petalburg Woods Team Aqua, Route 110/118/119/121 rival /
Steven / Aqua triggers, and the Meteor Falls / Mt Pyre / Seafloor Cavern /
Victory Road / Sky Pillar set-pieces.

Rest each at 1 ('you've passed this beat') — verified each var's coord and
onFrame gates exclude 1, so no later scene is enabled. Functional,
self-resolving events (New Mauville locked door, museum entry fee, Trick
House flavor) and unconditional weather triggers are left to fire.

Verified: seeded player triggers none of the 19 swept maps (0 traps / 0
unresolved); forcing a var to 0 still fires its block + resolves + completes;
test_ow_hoenn 12/12.

entries.title: overworld: ship Johto (Crystal) coord_events + scene-var seeding
entries.body:
Crystal's intro/story triggers live in coord_events gated on a per-map
scene var (VAR_SCENE_<Map>); the Crystal map parser had hardcoded
coord_events:[] so all 104 (across 37 maps) were missing. Injected them
from the decomp with correct scene-index gating.

A region-picker already has a starter, so seed each map that has a
scene-0 coord_event to its NOOP/resting scene — otherwise walking onto a
trigger tile fires a forced intro cutscene (New Bark teacher dragging you
home, Mom's greeting, story blocks). Verified: seeded player triggers
nothing; forcing scene 0 still fires the teacher block, resolves its text,
and completes; Johto opening path (9 maps) has 0 traps / 0 unresolved.

entries.title: overworld: drop dead STORY_SEED lab var, document lab scene seed
entries.body:
VAR_MAP_SCENE_OAKS_LAB was seeded but referenced by no shipped script
(wrong name). The real lab scene var is
VAR_MAP_SCENE_PALLET_TOWN_PROFESSOR_OAKS_LAB, intentionally left at its
default 0 so a starter-holding region-picker skips both the ChooseStarter
(1) and NationalDex (7) onFrame scenes and walks into a normal lab.

entries.title: Cross-file common-text resolution (all regions -> ~100%)
entries.body:
Scripts reference text defined outside their own map (cross-map <Other>_Text_*,
global gText_*, shared UI strings). A new resolver scans the decomp corpora and
ships only the referenced-but-unresolved labels as strings/_common.json (814
entries). resolveText falls back to it after the per-map strings, taking text
resolution from 87% to ~100% (remaining gaps are dynamic runtime buffers).

entries.title: Extend story coverage to Hoenn (Emerald)
entries.body:
- Transpiler now handles Emerald's single-colon local labels (movement lists),
  turnobject/setobjectxy; text resolves from scripts.inc too (Emerald inlines
  .string defs rather than a separate text.inc)
- Ship Kanto + Hoenn scripts/strings (FireRed then Emerald; shared-name maps
  take the Hoenn version) and a merged trainer_teams.json (1486 trainers)
- events.js handles a generic face(who,dir) op
- Stage 4: Hoenn STORY_SEED advances the Littleroot scene vars so Birch's
  edge-block doesn't stop a starter-holding player

entries.title: Canonical scripted trainer teams + Stage 4 story-seeding
entries.body:
- Ship trainer_teams.json: TRAINER_id -> canonical party (species/level/moves)
  from the FireRed decomp, 632 trainers / 1637 mons
- startScriptedBattle prefers the canonical team by TRAINER_id (exact roster +
  movesets), falling back to the script-label roster then a class-pool team
- Stage 4: seedStoryState on a new game advances the scene vars that gate the
  linear intro, so a player who picked a starter via region-select isn't blocked
  by the "Oak stops you leaving without a Pokemon" trigger at Pallet's edge

entries.title: Story engine: wire scripted trainer battles to battle.startTrainer
entries.body:
The trainerbattle opcode now runs a real battle instead of auto-winning. The
interpreter expands trainerbattle_single into its sequence (intro text -> battle
-> defeat text on win -> post-battle script), and startScriptedBattle builds the
foe party (canonical roster keyed by the running script label, else a class-pool
team at the map's level), runs battle.startTrainer, and resumes the cutscene
with the result in VAR_RESULT: a win continues the script; a loss stops it and
heals the party.

entries.title: Story engine Stage 3: Kanto special-command handlers
entries.body:
runSpecial now handles the special commands scripts branch on: GetBattleOutcome
(scripted battles treated as wins for now), party count/species/friendship,
Pokedex counts, IsNationalPokedexEnabled, HealPlayerParty, and the party/daycare
pickers. Store-writing queries set their result var (or VAR_RESULT by the decomp
convention when a plain `special` is used); any unhandled store-special defaults
to 0 so branches take the deterministic "nothing happened" path instead of
misfiring on a stale var. Cosmetic specials (map redraw, screen shake, camera,
quest-log) no-op.

entries.title: Story engine Stage 2: run ported Kanto map scripts
entries.body:
The events.js interpreter is now label-addressable with a call stack, running
the transpiled opcode set (control flow goto/call/return/branch, movement,
flags/vars, warps, item/mon gifts, hide/show objects, special dispatch). main.js
loads each map's scripts/strings, runs ON_TRANSITION setup on entry, ON_FRAME
auto-cutscenes and coord_event tile triggers on step, and object_event scripts
on talk — resolving msg labels to text via the strings map ({PLAYER} tokens
substituted at runtime). Kanto (FireRed) data ships: 359 script maps.

Guards: ON_TRANSITION is setup-only (bails at any waiting op); ON_FRAME value-0
entries don't fire from a blank save; unknown ops/specials no-op so scripts
never hang.

entries.title: Story engine: persisted flags/vars + a cutscene interpreter
entries.body:
Foundation for porting the decomp's progression/cutscenes. events.js holds a
persisted flag/var store (magepunk_story) and a Cutscene runner that steps an
opcode list — lock input, sequence dialogue, walk NPCs/player tile-by-tile,
set flags/vars, give items/mons, branch on flags. A running cutscene freezes
player input and menus.

Wired into the loop with a one-time new-game welcome cutscene (dialogue +
starter-kit gift + intro flag) as a working demo. The opcode format is designed
to be transpiler-friendly for the map scripts.inc (~96% of decomp script
commands are mechanical: movement, msgbox, setvar/flag, branch, trainer battle).

entries.title: Options screen: text speed, sound, auto-run, day/night
entries.body:
- settings.js (magepunk_settings): persisted options with cycle/get/set and
  derived helpers (volumeMult, charsPerSec)
- Options menu replaces the one-line stub: rows with a value + ◄► chevrons,
  arrows or tap to change, saves automatically
- Text-speed drives a dialog typewriter (slow/mid/fast/instant): text reveals
  over time, first Z reveals the rest of the page, ▼ only shows when complete
- Sound setting scales cry/SFX volume (off/low/mid/full) in sound.js
- Auto-run: player runs without holding Shift; Day & Night: toggles the tint

entries.title: Daycare + breeding, and the utility NPCs (move deleter/reminder, name rater)
entries.body:
- daycare.js (magepunk_daycare): deposit up to two mons; they gain EXP per
  walked step and recompute level/stats on withdrawal (fee scales with levels
  gained). A compatible pair (opposite genders, or a Ditto) lays an Egg after
  ~128 steps that incubates while you walk and hatches into the mother's
  base-form baby at Lv5
- Daycare front-desk menu on the Day Care maps (Kanto/Route5/Route117/Four
  Island): deposit / take back / collect egg
- Move Services on the Move Deleter's House maps: forget a move (keeps the last
  one) and recall a past level-up move (relearner), reusing the forget picker
  when all four slots are full
- Name Rater on the Name Rater maps: rename a party mon (sets its display name;
  blank reverts to the species name)
- Step hook in player.onArrive drives daycare EXP + egg incubation

entries.title: Day-night clock + time-based evolutions
entries.body:
- clock.js: accelerated in-game clock (24 real min = 1 day) from the wall
  clock; phases morning/day/night, hour/frac/label, test override
- Day-night colour wash over the overworld (multiply overlay keyed to the
  in-game hour, smooth dawn/dusk ramps); indoor maps stay untinted
- Time-gated evolutions: species_extra evos now carry time: day|night (from
  the Showdown evoCondition); evolution.check only fires a timed evo when the
  clock phase matches — Eevee->Espeon by day, Umbreon by night (21 evos tagged)
- Trainer Card shows the current time + phase

entries.title: Town Map: authentic region art behind the fly dots
entries.body:
- Export kanto.png (FireRed, 240x160) + johto.png (Crystal, 160x144) into
  overworld/data/townmap; export_web_data.py copies them going forward
- flydata.js: per-region image metadata + marker-pixel coords — Kanto/JohKanto
  use the FireRed grid formula (8*col+36, 8*row+36), Johto uses authentic
  landmark pixels; Hoenn stays a procedural dot map
- drawTownMap draws the region image letterboxed in the panel (nearest-neighbor)
  and places the town dots on the baked city markers

entries.title: Fly + Town Map
entries.body:
- flydata.js: 46 fly destinations across 4 regions (Kanto/Johto/Kanto-Past/
  Hoenn) with landing tiles + town-map grid positions, ported from the Lua
  game's FlyDestinations.lua + TownMapLayout.lua
- Visited-town tracking (magepunk_flypoints): a town registers as a fly point
  when you first stand on it (incl. the starting town)
- Town Map menu: canvas panel with town dots at their regional grid positions,
  a cursor, region tabs (Kanto/Johto/Kanto-Past/Hoenn), visited=bright /
  unvisited=dim, and a FLY HERE action; opens to the current region
- flyTo warps straight to a town's landing tile (nearest walkable), confirm
  dialog first; can only fly to visited towns
- START menu gains a TOWN MAP entry

entries.title: Strength: pushable boulders
entries.body:
- Parse OBJ_EVENT_GFX_BOULDER / PUSHABLE_BOULDER (141 across 36 maps) into
  solid field objects with a rounded boulder sprite
- Player movement hook: bumping a boulder shoves it one tile ahead when a
  party mon knows or can learn Strength and the far tile is open floor; the
  player then steps into the vacated tile
- First bump with no Strength user shows a hint instead
- Boulders reset per map visit (not persisted), so puzzles can't soft-lock

entries.title: Info menus: Pokédex, party summary, Trainer Card, mart selling
entries.body:
- pokedex.js: persistent seen/caught tracking (magepunk_dex_v1), recorded on
  battle start and catch, seeded from party+box on boot
- Browsable Pokédex menu sorted by dex number (fakemon after the standard dex),
  seen/caught marks, detail view with sprite/types/base-stat bars
- Party summary screen: portrait, types, ability, held item, friendship, six
  stat bars, and the four moves with type/PP; MAKE LEAD promotes the mon
- Trainer Card: name, region, money, dex seen/caught, party size, playtime
  (playtime accumulator + region persisted on starter pick)
- Mart BUY/SELL toggle; selling yields half price

entries.title: Overworld content: fishing, TMs, stone/friendship evolutions, rock smash + cut
entries.body:
- Fishing rods (Old/Good/Super) cast from the bag facing water; rod tier
  reads the map's fishing table slot bands (0-1 / 2-4 / 5-9), 103 maps
- TM teaching from the bag: Gen3 TM/HM tables + name-embedded ids, species
  learn-compat check, forget-a-move picker; consumed on use
- Evolution stones + trade items (Linking Cord etc.) usable on party members;
  full evo data now exported (item/friendship/trade, not just level)
- Friendship stat on mons, grows with wins/level-ups; friendship evos on check
- Breakable rocks (44) and cuttable trees (33) as solid field objects; Rock
  Smash rolls the rock_smash encounter table (19 maps)
- Shop stocks rods, all evolution stones, and the Linking Cord

entries.title: Battle robustness: fix save corruption from Transform-class moves + 8 more bugs
entries.body:
- Snapshot/restore stats/types/ability (Transform, Imposter, Trace, Power
  Trick/Split, Speed Swap, Soak, Conversion, Skill Swap, etc. permanently
  corrupted the saved party)
- Sleep Talk works (called moves skip beforeMove; no double status rolls)
- Sleep/freeze resolve before confusion/attract in beforeMove
- Substitute blocks secondaries/contact procs/item theft; sound bypasses
- Typed status moves respect type immunity (Thunder Wave vs Ground)
- Secondary statuses respect ability immunities (Water Veil etc.)
- Destiny Bond expires on the user's next action; Fake Out added
- POWER_FX: Gyro Ball, Electro Ball, Flail/Reversal, Eruption/Water Spout,
  Hex, Facade, Brine, Stored Power, Punishment, Acrobatics, Knock Off,
  Smelling Salts/Wake-Up Slap, Return, Weather Ball (power+type), Solar Beam
- Thunder/Hurricane/Blizzard weather accuracy; Quick Claw works in Trick Room

entries.title: Corrupt keyword (Darkmoon Faire)
entries.body:
A Corrupt card upgrades in hand the moment you play a card that costs
MORE than it. One-shot cards swap to a registered corrupted token form
(`corrupt` = that id); Horrendous Growth grows +1/+1 endlessly in place
(`corruptGrow`). All eligible Corrupt cards in hand corrupt from a single
costlier play. Hooked into playCard via corruptHandCards.

Adds 9 base cards + 8 corrupted forms with art: Horrendous Growth,
Strongman, Fleethoof Pearltusk, Darkmoon Dirigible, Firework Elemental,
Circus Medic, Dancing Cobra, Darkmoon Statue, Carnival Clown. Verified
by a 20-case suite + a 40-game smoke (685 plays, 0 errors). Pool regen'd.

entries.title: Overheal keyword + MTG-style hero healing (no life cap)
entries.body:
Overheal fires when a heal overflows past a creature's full Health:
new `overheal` effect field on instances, evaluated in healCreature via
the overflow amount. Adds 5 Priest creatures (Holy Champion, Mana Geode,
Crimson Clergy, Injured Hauler, Heartbreaker Hedanis) with art.

Heroes now heal above their starting life with no ceiling (MTG rules):
healHero no longer clamps to maxLife. Grammar + pool regenerated.

entries.title: Spellburst: keyword-peel + inner-effect grammar, with art
entries.body:
Engine: double-attack-self, refresh-mana ops; frozen-enemy-creatures damage
target. Pool 2477 -> 2488, full art; MP pool refreshed. 25-game smoke 0 errors.

entries.title: Bombs: draw-detonation + shuffle/scaling ops, with art
entries.body:
Engine: Bomb explodes on draw (5 to that hero) in drawCards; shuffle-bomb and
summon-per-enemy-bomb ops; Bomb + Boom Bot tokens; fixed Blastmaster Boom.
Pool 2470 -> 2477, full art; MP pool refreshed. 25-game smoke 0 errors.

entries.title: C'Thun: cross-zone buff tracker + scaling Battlecry, with art
entries.body:
Engine: cthunAtk/cthunHp/cthunTaunt per-player; syncCthun keeps any C'Thun in
hand/board at 6/6 + tracker; buff-cthun, cthun-blast ops; cthunMinAttack cond;
C'Thun buffs apply on draw from deck. Pool 2457 -> 2470, full art; MP pool
refreshed. 25-game smoke 0 errors.

entries.title: Add playable 'hero' card type; Galakrond uses it
entries.body:
New card type 'hero': on play, gain Armor, run the Battlecry, and add the card's
Hero Power to a free slot WITHOUT replacing your original (this game has multiple
hero-power slots). The hero card itself is spent. instantiate now carries armor.
Galakrond's 5 cards are type 'hero'. Verified: keeps original power + adds
Galakrond's, gains 5 Armor, battlecry scales, card consumed; 30-game smoke 0 errors.

entries.title: Galakrond: 5 hero cards with scaling battlecries + Invoke keyword, with art
Early-sets sweep: +13 cards with art; trigger-one-deathrattle + random-friendly bounce
entries.body:
Engine: trigger-one-deathrattle op (fire a chosen friendly creature's Deathrattle),
bounce random-friendly target, undamaged-creature damage. Pool 2430 -> 2443, full
art; MP pool refreshed. 25-game smoke 0 errors.

entries.title: Colossal complete: Cho'gall + Sinestra (24/24)
entries.body:
Engine: destroy-right-gain enemy-deck mode (Cho'gall); off-class spell recast
with a recasting guard (Sinestra). Pool 2426 -> 2430, full art; MP pool refreshed.
All 24 Colossal legendaries play with correct effects. 30-game smoke 0 errors.

entries.title: Herald-scaled Colossals (+4): appendages read live Herald count
entries.body:
Engine: heraldMult + heraldScaled effect support (random-damage, hero-temp-attack,
conjure-cost, conjure-named, adjacent aura); onSummon appendage effects; body ops
heroWindfury, conjure-by-attack, healToMaxHealth. 18 of 24 Colossals now play with
correct effects. Pool 2420 -> 2426, full art; MP pool refreshed. 30-game smoke 0 errors.

entries.title: Herald keyword: 6 scaling class Soldiers + 8 Herald cards, with art
entries.body:
Engine: heraldCount per player; herald op summons the caller's class Soldier
scaled x1/x2/x4 by Herald count; destroy-right-gain op for the Warlock Soldier.
Pool 2406 -> 2420, full art coverage; MP pool refreshed. 30-game smoke 0 errors.

entries.title: Colossal creatures: 14 legendaries with faithful effects + appendages, with art
entries.body:
The Colossal +N mechanic summons N appendage tokens as the creature enters play
(before its battlecry), per the wiki. 14 of the 24 Colossal legendaries now play
with correct effects; each appendage token carries its own abilities.

New engine ops (all generic): summonColossalParts, creature-frozen + friendly-
attacks trigger events, colossal/colossalOf/immuneWhile/partPower fields,
conjure-named costMod, random-damaged-friendly heal, and gain-dead-stats,
buff-colossal, remove-colossal-keyword, grant-colossal-parts, destroy-random-
per-part, destroy-triggering, attack-random-enemy, trigger-deathrattles,
summon-if-control, force-attack, stalk-strike, boost-parts-power.

Cards: Chromatus, Vulcanos, Wickerfang, Glugg, Ozumat, Frost Queen Sindragosa,

entries.title: Jade Golem + Outcast engine support: +25 cards with art

Engine:

entries.title: Full-set HS sweep: +53 cards with art; generalized damage/discover/summon ops
entries.body:
Engine (all generic, reused across the sweep):
- Lifesteal on damage/random-damage effects heals the caster's hero by the real

Pool 2302 -> 2355, full art coverage (index 2363); MP realm pool refreshed.

entries.title: CATACLYSM import: +2 HS cards with art; bounce enemy-creatures target
entries.body:
Engine: bounce gains an 'enemy-creatures' target (mass bounce that spares your

Verified: Twilight Mistress bounces only enemy creatures back to their owner's

entries.title: Violet Hold import: +31 HS cards with art; conjure-named filters + class-sparing wipe
entries.body:
Engine: conjure-named gains optional cardType/cardClass filters (and skips
tokens); destroy-all gains exceptClass/exceptTribe ('Destroy all non-Paladin
creatures'). Pool 2269 -> 2300; all 30 new-art cards fetched from the
HearthstoneJSON CDN (index 2308, full coverage).

Verified: Contraband Wands conjures exactly 3 Arcane Missiles, Cold Snap
freezes + conjures a Frost spell, V'ama spares only Paladin creatures,
Secret Ingredient's inline choose-one branches; 15-game smoke, 0 errors.
Also re-verified the 3 adventure cards cast-and-return properly (the earlier
force-test drew from the wrong end of the deck and validated nothing).

entries.title: Multiplayer test #1 fixes: ghost interpolation, turn sequencing, duel diagnostics
entries.body:
Fixes for the three bugs from the first live 2-player test (full diagnosis in
Plans/MULTIPLAYER_FIX_PLAN.md):

Overworld ghosts (clipping/flicker):
- Waypoint queue + constant-speed interpolation (walk pace, run-catch-up when
  2+ tiles behind) replaces ease-snap to the last reported tile.
- Facing derives from travel direction; subtle step bob while moving.
- Grace period: a ghost survives 3 missed polls before deletion (instant delete
  on one missed poll caused the 'glimpse him every few frames' flicker).
- Server: the friends action reads all friend+presence blobs in parallel
  (was 2 sequential strong-consistency reads per friend).

Pokemon PvP ('we both moved at the same time'):
- resolveTurn announces '<mon> moves first!' when both sides move.
- Heals emit negative-dmg markers like damage already did.
- Client walks the turn's events IN ORDER: strings scroll as messages and each
  {hit,side,dmg} marker steps that side's HP bar when reached — pre-turn HP is
  reconstructed exactly by undoing the queued markers. Bars no longer snap to
  the final result while messages lag behind.

Card duel (guest 'never loaded' — not reproducible locally OR against prod;
two-client harness passes both, so likely device/timing-specific):
- tools/mp-duel-repro.cjs: automated 2-client repro (mp-dev-server or --prod,
  two headless Edge contexts, full challenge->accept->board->relay assertion).
- Host: publish failures are now counted and surfaced (CONNECTION LOST banner
  after 3 consecutive, auto-recovery notice) instead of .catch(()=>{}).
- Guest: snapshot-ingest exceptions are caught and logged on-screen (were
  silently killing the board build forever); the waiting screen shows elapsed
  time + last poll status after 10s.
- ?debug=1 overlay on duels: role, seq, publish/poll ages, error counts.

puppeteer-core added as a dev dependency for the harness.

entries.title: restore The Coin as a card + tooltip Modifiers section
entries.body:
The Coin card def (a 0-cost core token granting +1 temp mana) had been dropped
from cards.json — the paper importer writes the Magepunk66 card list to BOTH
copies, and that list never carried the coin, so every import clobbered it. With
the def gone, addCoin fell back to the legacy p.coins counter + button. Restored
the def; addCoin now hands out the real card again. Also export addCoin and use
it on multiplayer guest-join (was setting the legacy counter). The old button
self-hides (nothing increments p.coins anymore).

Modifiers section: the hover tooltip now lists keywords a creature has gained but
didn't start with (buffs/auras/grants), plus its stat swing vs. the printed body
(e.g. 'Modifiers — +2/+1, Taunt, Divine Shield'). Computed against the card def
in cardsById; pristine cards show nothing. New keywordLabel() export maps engine
tags to display names.

entries.title: correct dual/multi-class on HS cards (24 re-classed)
entries.body:
Dual/tri/multi-class HS cards now carry our 'a__b' class encoding so the
deck-builder offers them to each of their classes. Faithful-only: 110 cards
whose abilities need unimplemented mechanics are left out, not shipped broken.

entries.title: adventure cards + grammar sweep (+41 cards)
entries.body:
Grammar improvements to the paper/HS importers unlock more of both pools:
- Adventures: fix name extraction for type-first typelines ("Sorcery —
  Adventure" with the name on the previous line); +3 adventure creatures
  (Frolicking Familiar, Mothwood Direcat, Steady Tortoise), each a creature
  with a castable spell half.
- Enchantments: run the global-enchantment handler for subtyped cards
  (gate on "Enchant creature/Hero" local auras, not on having any subtype);
  +Incanter's Flow and other cost/control auras.
- Locations: fix the tap-line regex (the char class was eating the '&' before
  'Remove a Durability', so every multi-durability location failed to match).
- Two generalizing summon primitives ("Summon a random <race>", bare
  "Summon a N/N <name>") that the engine already executes.

The HS bridge re-scan picks up 34 newly-parseable cards from these; paper adds
7. Pool 2227 -> 2268.

Engine: Adventure subsystem (dual-mode creature+spell) — instantiate fields,
resolveEntry 'adventure' dispatch, adventureSpec/canPlayAdventure/playAdventure.
game.js: openAdventureMenu (Summon vs Cast), commitPending 'adventure' mode,
actAdventure + guest relay. Validated: 40-game smoke (2386 plays) + forced
play of every adventure (both modes) and enchantment, 0 errors.

entries.title: Bridge the HS json through the paper grammar: +311 cards
entries.body:
The HS importer used its original limited grammar (yielded 1 new card from
7259). New tools/import_hs_bridge.py synthesizes each collectible HS minion/
spell/weapon into the paper input format (strip HTML, collapse newlines,
minion->creature, build type line) and runs it through import_paper_cards.
convert(), which now understands every mechanic we've added.

Adds 311 new functional HS cards (marked set:'hs'); 92 that parsed but whose
static/cost-reduction text we can't implement yet are skipped as inert rather
than imported as misleading near-vanilla bodies. Paper cards are never
overwritten (id collisions skipped). Deck: 2227 cards.

Verified: engine loads the full pool and builds decks.

entries.title: Attacks open a priority window (combat tricks) + deeper reactive AI
entries.body:
Attacks now use the stack: attack() declares the swing (attacksUsed, Swing/
Sanguine/defender-secrets/redirect all still fire), then the combat damage is
deferred to resolveCombat() through stackAction, so opponents get an instant-
speed window before damage. resolveCombat re-validates — if the attacker (or
target) died in the window, the swing fizzles. Lazy as ever: with no possible
response, combat resolves inline exactly as before.

AI: aiChooseResponse now gathers instant-speed damage sources (instants AND
creature abilities), and (1) counters worthwhile spells, (2) when defending an
attack, kills the attacker to blow out the swing, (3) otherwise removes the
biggest worthwhile enemy creature — always with the cheapest sufficient source.

game.js stackPush log is action-aware (attack/ability/land/hero-power/spell).

Verified: normal combat resolves inline; a combat trick (kill the attacker in
response) fizzles the swing; passing resolves combat normally.

entries.title: Instant vs sorcery speed: a general priority system
entries.body:
Turns the spell-only stack into a general instant/sorcery-speed system.

Speed rules:
- Sorcery speed (sorceries, creatures, hero powers, planeswalker abilities,
  attacks): only on your turn with an empty stack and no open window.
- Instant speed (instants, creature activated abilities, all land abilities):
  usable whenever you hold priority — on your turn OR in response to anything.
  Abilities/lands are instant speed by default (a.sorcerySpeed opts out).

Engine: hasPriority(); creature abilities, land taps, and hero powers now route
through the stack via stackAction(); resolveTop dispatches by kind; responses
(resolveResponse) can be an instant spell, an activated ability, or a land tap,
each of which stacks on top and re-opens priority (LIFO). Lazy as always — an
action only pauses if an opponent actually holds an instant-speed response, so
the ~1900-card common path resolves inline.

UI: an Auto-pass toggle (default ON = instantly pass); turn it OFF to get a
4-second window to respond, with the respond modal now listing instants,
creature abilities, and land abilities (targeted ones route through targeting).
Windows open whenever you gain priority, not just on spell casts.

AI: value-driven responses — counters spells that are expensive or aimed at it,
fires a removal/burn instant that would kill a worthwhile enemy creature, and
otherwise holds priority.

Verified: common spells resolve inline; sorcery speed is gated off-turn; a
creature ability resolves in response to a spell (LIFO, then the spell); normal
play (creature/hero power/attack/end turn) all still work.

entries.title: Add counter cards: Castblock, Mana Bind, Time Stop
entries.body:
Now that the stack exists, three more spell-interaction cards from the paper
set are real:
- Castblock (Arcane Secret, 3): when an opponent casts a spell, Counter it.
- Mana Bind (Arcane Secret, 3): Counter it and add a 0-cost copy to your hand
  (new `copy-spell` secret effect that clones the triggering spell).
- Time Stop (Instant, 5): a Counter that also ends the turn (new `end-turn`
  effect).

The two secrets reuse the existing enemy-spell-cast trigger + `counter` effect,
firing when the spell resolves; Time Stop is a counterSpell instant cast in a
priority window. Deck: 1916 cards.

Verified: Castblock and Mana Bind fizzle an enemy spell (Mana Bind hands you a
free copy); Time Stop counters and ends the caster's turn.

entries.title: Stack v2: real priority — counter a counter, cast any instant in response
entries.body:
Replaces the single-response window with a proper MTG-style priority loop:
- state.priority / passers / priorityNext drive round-robin priority; when all
  players pass, the top of the stack resolves (LIFO), then a fresh round opens
  on the new top.
- Counter-wars work: countering a counter lets the original spell resolve. A
  Counter targets the entry directly below it; resolving removes that entry.
- Any INSTANT (not just Counters) can be cast in response; sorceries still only
  cast on your turn. resolveResponse(pi, cardUid, target, choice) casts it onto
  the stack. Lazy as before: a spell only stacks if an opponent can actually
  respond, so the 1900-card common path resolves inline untouched.

Engine: offerPriority/resolveTop/stackSpell/canCastInResponse/canRespond +
responseOptions. Game: AI still auto-counters costly spells (loops through every
priority window); the human respond modal now lists all castable instants —
Counters/no-target one-click, targeted instants route through the normal
targeting UI (new commitPending 'respond' mode); snapshots + guest relay carry
priority/passers.

Verified: common spells resolve inline; simple counter fizzles a spell; A
counters B's counter so the original resolves; a non-counter instant resolves
LIFO above the pending spell and re-opens priority.

entries.title: Add the stack + counterspells
entries.body:
Spells now go on a stack when an opponent can respond, instead of always
resolving instantly. A spell only stacks if an opponent actually holds an
affordable Counter — otherwise it resolves inline exactly as before, so the
whole existing card pool is unaffected.

Engine: state.stack + respondQueue; resolveStackedSpell (extracted spell
resolution); counterResponders/counterOptions/pendingSpellFor; resolveResponse
(pass or counter). A card flagged counterSpell, played in response, counters
the pending spell (sent to graveyard, never resolves). New Counterspell card
(instant, 3, "Counter target spell").

Game: AI auto-responds (counters spells costing 3+), a human counter window
(modal offering each held Counter or Pass), stackPush log, the AI pauses while
you hold priority, plus guest relay + duel snapshot/modal for multiplayer.

v1 scope: a single response window (first counter wins); "countering a counter"
and instant-speed responses beyond counters are future work. Deck: 1913.

Verified: no-counter spells resolve inline; a held Counter stacks the spell;
passing resolves it, countering fizzles it; AI counters costly spells, passes
cheap ones.

entries.title: Each player may Spark (Celestial Dreamer)
entries.body:
The `spark` effect gains target 'all' — every player Sparks (always beneficial,
so auto-taken), unlocking each of their planar dice. Importer parses "Each
player may Spark". Unlocks Celestial Dreamer (Battlecry: if you control a 5+
Attack creature, +2/+2; Deathrattle: each player may Spark). Deck: 1913.

Verified: its deathrattle sparks both players; the opponent can then Planeswalk
on their turn; the battlecry buffs only when a 5+ Attack creature is controlled.

entries.title: Add the planar die (Planeswalk) + Spark + plane Chaos
entries.body:
Planeswalk rolls a d6 as a bonus "hero power" that never counts toward the 3
hero-power limit. You may roll only if you control a planeswalker or have used
Spark. First roll each turn is free; each further roll costs 1 more generic
mana. d6: 6 = Planeshift (old plane's Departure fires, a new plane Arrives),
5 = Chaos (the active plane's Chaos ability), 1-4 = nothing.

Engine: canPlaneswalk/planeswalk/planarRollCost actions, `spark` effect
(p.sparked), per-turn roll counter reset at turn start, `sacrifice-each` +
destroy-all `tribe` filter + mill target 'all' for Chaos, and
`shuffle-self-into-deck` (Astral Tiger). Each plane gains a Chaos ability.
UI: a Planeswalk button (shows the escalating cost) mirroring the Coin button,
with guest relay + roll/spark/coin-flip log lines. Importer parses Spark and
"Shuffle this card back into your deck" (unlocks Astral Tiger). Glossary added.
Deck: 1912.

Verified: gating (needs planeswalker or Spark); roll 6 planeshifts; cost goes
free -> 1 -> 2; roll 5 fires the plane's Chaos (Alara sac-each); rolls reset
each turn.

entries.title: Implement the continuous plane statics
entries.body:
Each active plane now applies its middle-line static via a `staticRule` on the
plane card, consulted at the relevant engine hooks:

- Zendikar: Enchantment spells cost 1 less (effectiveCost).
- Alkabah: Instants & Sorceries that cost 4 cost 0 (effectiveCost).
- Belenon: Lands & Locations don't untap at turn start (untap loop guarded).
- Alara: start-of-turn coin flip blocks odd- or even-cost plays this turn
  (turn-start flip sets parityBlock; canPlay enforces it).
- Primordia: playing a creature auto-sacrifices a spare token artifact for
  +2/+2 (never a hand-made artifact).
- Bloomburrow's "Humans can't attack" (noAttackTribe) already shipped.

Flash (Zendikar) and Chaos (planar die) are still omitted — we have no
instant-speed play or planar die. Descriptions updated to match. Deck: 1911.

Verified each: 4-cost spell -> 0 under Alkabah; enchant -1 under Zendikar;
odd-cost blocked under Alara; land stays tapped under Belenon; creature gains
+2/+2 (token sacrificed) under Primordia.

entries.title: Add Planeshift + arena planes
entries.body:
Planeshift shifts the arena to a random different plane — the old plane's
Departure fires, the new one's Arrival fires. `state.plane` is shared arena
state (nobody controls it), null until the first Planeshift. Persists across
turns. New engine bits: the `planeshift` effect, `draw` target 'all' (each
player draws), `buff` target 'all-creatures' with `exceptTribe`, and a plane
`noAttackTribe` static checked in canAttackWith.

Six planes authored as uncollectible arena cards (tools/_gen_planes.py):
- Alkabah (gain 5 life all / 3 dmg all creatures)
- Bloomburrow (Non-Humans +3/+3, Humans can't attack / 2 dmg all creatures)
- Primordia (draw all / gain 2 life all)
- Alara, Belenon, Zendikar (Arrival importable; their continuous statics and
  multi-player discover/dredge are simplified for now)
Chaos (planar-die) is omitted — we have no die. Importer parses "Planeshift"
(unlocks Interstellar Stowaway, Mica Wanderknight, Omenpath Drake); glossary +
a planeshift log line added. Deck: 1911 cards.

Verified: plane starts null; a Planeshift sets a random plane and fires its
arrival (heal/draw); a second departs the old (damage) and arrives the new;
Bloomburrow blocks Human attacks.

entries.title: Fix Morkrut Behemoth
entries.body:
Two new pieces let it import fully:
- `pay-or-sacrifice` effect: "sacrifice this unless you pay N" pays from leftover
  mana if able at end of turn, otherwise destroys the source.
- `noFriendlyDeaths` conditional: true when no creature you control died this turn.

Importer learns "Gain <keyword>" (self-grant, e.g. Gain Divine Shield),
"Sacrifice this creature unless you pay N", and "If no creatures you control
died this turn, ...". Morkrut's Avenge (in ongoings) and end-of-turn upkeep (in
ongoing) coexist. Deck: 1902 cards.

Verified: Avenge grants Divine Shield on a friendly death; with no friendly
deaths it is sacrificed at 0 mana but survives (paying 3) at 5 mana; and it
survives whenever a friendly creature died that turn.

entries.title: Fix Avenge: repeatable, and stackable with other triggers
entries.body:
Avenge N fires every time N creatures you control die — repeatable, not a
one-shot. Was `{need, once}` (fired once ever), which made growth cards like
Flag Runner ("Avenge 1: Gain +1 Attack" on a 1/6) pointless; now `{every: N}`
so it re-arms. Avenge and Morbid now route into the `ongoings` array, so a card
can carry both (or Avenge plus another trigger).

Unlocks/repairs Flag Runner, Scavenger Drake, Windsoul Automaton, Wraith of
Enochia and Ancalagon (Avenge 1 + Morbid 1 coexisting). The Adapt-table Avenge
option is repeatable to match. Deck: 1901 cards.

Verified: Flag Runner +1 Attack on each friendly death; Windsoul (Avenge 3)
fires only on the 3rd death.

entries.title: Finish Flame Leviathan: tribe-excluded damage
entries.body:
The damage effect's all-creatures / enemy-creatures targets gain an
`exceptTribe` filter, so "Deal N damage to all Non-<Tribe> creatures" spares
that tribe. Importer parses the phrasing. Unlocks Flame Leviathan (Rush;
Emerge: Deal 2 to all Non-Mech creatures) — the last Emerge holdout. Deck: 1900.

Verified: its Emerge hits every non-Mech on both boards for 2 and leaves Mechs
untouched.

entries.title: Support combined triggers (multiple triggers, one effect)
entries.body:
Cards like "Emerge & Frenzy: Deal 4" or "Battlecry, Inspire, Spellburst,
Frenzy & Honorable Kill: Gain +2/+2" fire one effect on several triggers. A
card previously had a single `ongoing` slot; fireOngoing now also walks an
`ongoings` array, so a creature can hold any number of triggered abilities.
Per-trigger once/need/every counters moved onto the trigger object (a
Spellburst can be spent while an Alliance on the same card keeps firing).

Importer parses a leading list of 2+ known triggers and routes the shared
effect to each slot: ongoing triggers (Inspire/Swing/Alliance/Spellburst/
Frenzy/Connect/Constellation/Ponder) into `ongoings`, plus Battlecry,
Deathrattle, Emerge, Finale and Honorable Kill into their own slots.

Unlocks 7 cards incl. Playful Predator (Emerge+Battlecry+Alliance+Spellburst+
Frenzy), Solarion (5 triggers), Cheerful Chomper, Sandstorm Sniper, Panda
Catfish, Second Little Pig, Lulu. Deck: 1899 cards.

Verified: multiple ongoings each fire on their own trigger with independent
once/repeat semantics; single-ongoing cards unchanged (regression pass).

cards.name: Lulu, Queen of the Summer Feast

entries.title: Add Emerge keyword
entries.body:
Emerge: a card's effect that fires from your hand the moment it is drawn or
discovered — but NOT from your opening hand. A `state.dealt` flag flips true
after the opening hands are dealt (before the turn-1 draw), and fireEmerge()
runs card.emerge at every real hand-entry point: draw, discover, conjure, and
add-to-hand. Guarded by a re-entrancy lock; instantiate now carries the emerge
field.

Importer parses "Emerge: X"; glossary entry added. Unlocks The Forgotten One
(Emerge: Destroy all creatures). Combined-trigger Emerge cards (Emerge & Frenzy,
etc.) and Flame Leviathan's "Non-Mech" filter remain blocked by unrelated gaps.
Deck: 1892 cards.

Verified: opening-hand cards do not fire; drawing and discovering do; The
Forgotten One wipes the board when drawn.

entries.title: Add Finale keyword
entries.body:
Finale: a play-time bonus that fires if you spent all your remaining mana to
play the card (availableMana === 0 when the effect resolves, since mana is paid
before the battlecry runs). New `finale` condition on the conditional effect.

Importer parses "Finale: X" as a play-time conditional; "Finale: X instead"
swaps out the base battlecry when Finale is active (else keeps it). Added a
"Deal N damage to all enemies" tail and a glossary entry.

Unlocks Hardcore Cultist (Battlecry: 2 to any; Finale: 2 to all enemies
instead). Other Finale cards stay blocked by unrelated text (multi-trigger
Adapt, per-mana-crystal scaling, a "your Finale effects trigger twice" static).
Deck: 1891 cards.

Verified both branches: all-mana-spent -> AoE to all enemies; mana left -> base
hits only the chosen target.

entries.title: Add Manathirst keyword
entries.body:
Manathirst (N): a bonus effect that activates once your mana crystals this turn
reach N, whether or not you've spent them. Implemented as a new `manathirst`
condition on the existing conditional effect (checks mana.max >= N). Importer
parses "Manathirst(N): X" / "(Manathirst N: X)"; glossary entry added.

Unlocks Consume Magic and Conjured Arrow; other Manathirst cards remain blocked
by unrelated text (trade-triggers, "each opponent does the same", cost-zero
riders, "instead" replacement). Deck: 1890 cards.

Verified: below N no bonus; at N with 0 unspent mana the bonus still fires.
